articles.title: Marvel Addresses the Greatest Flaw of Civil War 20 Years Later
articles.summary: In both movie and comic book forms, the greatest flaw of Civil War is that the conflict eventually ended. But thanks to a pivotal new series, that problem is finally being addressed 20 years later.
articles.body:
When it comes to modern comic book crossovers, few stories can rival Marvel's Civil War when it comes to impact and influence. There was rarely a more exciting time to be reading Marvel's comic book line than the summer and fall of 2006, as iconic heroes like Iron Man and Captain America battled it out on the page and Spider-Man made international headlines. You can take issue with Civil War's execution and the way it characterized certain key players, but the fun factor and the core appeal of the series' premise are undeniable. It's no wonder Marvel Studios adapted the series to great success with 2016's Captain America: Civil War movie.

There's just one problem with Civil War in both its original and MCU forms - its influence on the larger Marvel Universe eventually faded. The ideological conflict over superhuman registration faded without ever being truly resolved. But thanks to Avengers: Armageddon , Marvel is finally addressing that flaw 20 years later. Civil War is a story that arguably never should have ended, and now, it seems it never did.

Read on to learn more about how this new crossover has successfully revived the Civil War conflict two decades later, but beware of spoilers for Avengers: Armageddon #3 ahead!

Marvel Comics: Avengers - Armageddon Panel Image Gallery

Civil War certainly boasts a strong elevator pitch, if nothing else. The series explores what happens when the general public grows fed up with teams like the Avengers operating without governmental oversight. In the wake of a massive tragedy in Stamford, CT, a remorseful Iron Man leads the charge for the Superhuman Registration Act. Opposing him is his old buddy Captain America, who believes heroes need to be free to act without worrying about jurisdiction or jumping through procedural hoops. Personal freedom on one side, and security and accountability on the other. It was basically the perfect conflict for a post-9/11 Marvel Universe.

That ideological divide split the superhero community right down the middle, with some heroes flocking to Iron Man's pro-registration banner and others throwing their lot in with Cap's underground resistance. And perhaps the greatest success of Civil War is that it actually allowed one side (Team Iron Man) to triumph over the other. The Superhuman Registration Act became the law of the land in the Marvel Universe.

And, as MCU fans well remember, a similar conflict played out in Phase 3. Team Iron Man won the debate in Captain America: Civil War, leading to a new status quo where Cap and his allies became fugitives from the law.

But again, the issue with both versions of the story is that the effects of Civil War eventually faded. On the comics side, Marvel explored the long-term fallout of Civil War in subsequent crossovers like 2007’s World War Hulk and 2008’s Secret Invasion, with Iron Man eventually becoming disgraced and replaced in his role as S.H.I.E.L.D. director by Norman Osborn. In the end, Osborn himself was exposed and overthrown, leading to the general public accepting the return of a more traditional, registration-free Avengers team. After several years of turmoil, the Marvel Universe basically reverted to square one.

Similarly, the MCU no longer really feels the effects of Captain America: Civil War. The Sokovia Accords have been phased out, and the general public generally seems willing to accept the idea of heroes operating outside the law (see 2026’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day, where Tom Holland’s Spidey has become New York’s favorite darling despite being a one-man surveillance state). We’ve seen echoes of Civil War through plot points like Mayor Fisk’s anti-vigilante task force in Daredevil: Born Again, but that’s about it.

Frankly, it’s never made sense that the average Joe in either version of the Marvel Universe would simply forget about the idea of superhuman registration and move on. Is it really so unreasonable for ordinary civilians to expect a certain degree of transparency and accountability from these all-powerful super-beings? Does the fact that the Avengers saved the universe from Thanos in 2019’s Avengers: Endgame give them a permanent free pass? It’s never sat right that Marvel would just abandon the concept of superhero registration on either the comics or film side, rather than making registration a permanent part of the conversation going forward.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

Avengers: Armageddon - The New Civil War

Enter Avengers: Armageddon. This crossover has come on the scene 20 years after the original Civil War’s debut, and 10 years after the original sequel, Civil War II ( the less said about that book, the better ). Marvel isn’t actually calling this book Civil War III, but after reading issue #3, they might as well have used the name. This book is very much a spiritual sequel to the original Civil War, and I’m all for it.

In Armageddon, the Avengers again find themselves pulled between their responsibility to uphold the law and their duty as heroes. The series opens with Red Hulk and his gamma-powered soldiers invading the war-torn nation of Latveria and declaring it “New America.” The Avengers and Fantastic Four, along with Spider-Man, Wolverine, and former Captain America-turned-godlike hero David Colton, opt to respond to Red Hulk’s attack despite being expressly forbidden by the US government. That decision has caused a chaotic chain reaction of events that threatens to destabilize world peace and turn the public against the Avengers once more.

Colton himself is the architect behind much of that chaos, as he sets about unilaterally destroying the world’s nuclear stockpiles, Superman IV-style. Colton feels nothing but contempt for the Avengers, arguing that people with great power have the responsibility to use that power to make the world a better place. Meanwhile, a new wave of anti-Avengers resentment is brewing, with even Spider-Man questioning whether the world would be better off if superheroes faced more oversight. The series is putting a fresh spin on the same themes that were explored in the original Civil War, thereby proving that the argument over superhuman registration never fully went away.

As the series reaches its climax in issues #4 and 5, we’re going to see a real doomsday scenario play out. Already, Colton has sparked possible nuclear war by failing to eliminate every warhead in existence. Now Red Hulk has thrown his lot in with Russia’s Winter Guard, while the recently reconstituted S.H.I.E.L.D. has taken a stand against the Avengers and rebranded itself “Strategic Human Intelligence, Enforcement, and Logistic Defense.” There’s a world war brewing, and the Avengers are partly to blame.

It’s exciting to see a series finally pick up Civil War’s baton and carry it forward again. At long last, the concept of superhero accountability is at the forefront of the Marvel U. once more. Not in exactly the same way that Civil War presented it, but in a way that builds on that conflict and proves that the original story’s themes and ideas still very much resonate 20 years down the road.

And we already know the effects of this conflict aren’t limited to Avengers: Armageddon itself. This series directly sets the stage for Chip Zdarsky and Marco Checchetto’s relaunched Avengers comic, which sees a drastically different version of Earth’s Mightiest Heroes try to make a stand in a world that hates and fears them like never before.

Zdarsky teases that Spider-Man and his fellow Avengers will be very much dealing with the aftereffects of Armageddon and the question of responsibility in the new series, telling IGN, “Spidey is the poster boy for power and responsibility, so going into Avengers, he and every other hero are considering what that means."

I’m looking forward to a new status quo for Marvel’s comic book universe very much like the post-Civil War lineup in 2007, where heroes everywhere are forced to choose whether they can operate within the confines of the law. Everything we’ve seen of the upcoming Avengers comic suggests that this team will be underground fugitives, similar to how the New Avengers operated in opposition to Iron Man’s Mighty Avengers. That was easily one of the most creatively fruitful periods for the franchise of the past several decades. Why not draw inspiration from the post-Civil War Avengers line? There’s still so much material to mine there.

And, sooner or later, we can only hope that the MCU looks to stories like Avengers: Armageddon for inspiration. Just like the comics, it feels like there’s still so much room to explore the central ideas and conflicts that fueled Captain America: Civil War. Particularly with mutants like Sadie Sink’s Jean Grey now popping up, the general MCU public has to be growing more and more wary of the many unlicensed, unsanctioned superhumans running around. Rather than let the Civil War conflict fade into the background, there’s an opportunity to revive it and explore the sometimes tumultuous relationship the world has with its costumed defenders.

Civil War is nothing if not a great idea for a Marvel story. But like Pandora’s Box, once you open that lid, there’s no putting things back in order. Thankfully, Marvel seems to be belatedly realizing that fact in Avengers: Armageddon. The age-old battle between freedom and security rages on.

For more on the future of the Marvel Universe, learn all about the new symbiote hero known as The Amazing Venom and see what to expect from Kevin Smith's epic Star Wars/Marvel crossover .

articles.title: Australia says Roblox hasn’t fixed its child predator problem
articles.summary: Roblox is promising more changes to its child safety features after Australia’s online safety regulator found issues, including that adults could send connection requests to children.
articles.body: Roblox is promising more changes to its child safety features following testing from Australia’s online safety regulator, eSafety. eSafety has been looking into concerns that the company hasn’t been in compliance with Australia’s Online Safety Act, including “allegedly failing to have sufficient measures in place to prevent contact between adults and children under 16.” While Roblox has put some new safety measures in place, eSafety’s testing this year found that the platform “continued to put children at risk, including allowing contact between children and adult strangers.” eSafety’s testing found that: > adults could send connection requests to young Australian children without parental or carer consent;  > children and adults could view and respond to one another’s posts on forums outside game environments without parental or carer consent;  > children’s connections were visible to anyone on the Roblox platform; > children’s profiles and biographies, including account names, number and names of connections, avatar images, and non-sensitive biographical information such as their interests were visible to anyone on the Roblox platform, with no option to restrict the visibility of this information. Roblox believes it meets its Online Safety Act obligations, according to eSafety. But the company will be adding further safety measures that include: > preventing adults from contacting unknown children without parental consent > strengthening the account settings of children’s accounts so they are private by default > accessible reporting mechanisms that notify users of complaint outcomes  > engaging an independent third-party auditor to assess the effectiveness of its safety measures, including the deployment of its age-estimation measures. ”This undertaking follows constructive dialogue with eSafety, Australia’s online safety regulator, and reflects our commitment to working with regulators and policymakers around the world to help keep kids safe online,” Nicky Jackson Colaço, Roblox’s global head of public policy, says in a statement. “Our recent rollout of industry leading safety features on Roblox, including Roblox Kids and Select accounts tailored specifically for users under 16, is one of many examples of this commitment.” In the US, Roblox is under investigation by a Senate subcommittee and has been sued by multiple states over alleged child safety issues, though it has settled some state lawsuits. articles.title: Nitro Deck 2 Is Finally Out for Switch 2 on Friday
articles.summary: It's nearly here: the Nitro Deck 2 controller for Switch 2 is set to release August 28.
articles.body:
I love the Nintendo Switch 2. It’s like the original Switch, but it can actually play modern games made by companies other than Nintendo. But despite releasing eight years after the OG Switch, the Switch 2 has the same big problem as its predecessor: I find the Joy-Cons that come with it uncomfortable to use.

Thankfully, third-party accessory makers are finally swooping in to replace them. One of our favorite original Switch accessories was the Nitro Deck, but it's not compatible with Switch 2. Enter the Nitro Deck 2 from CRKD which, after numerous delays , is finally shipping on Friday, August 28 ( see it at Amazon ), in three color options, with an additional one available exclusively at CRKD . The Nitro Deck 2 is designed to make the Switch 2 feel more comfortable in your hands.

The big new feature in this model versus the original Nitro Deck is that you can use it on the Switch 2 in handheld mode, or you can collapse it into a standard controller and use it to play in docked mode. That makes it twice as useful and minimizes the number of controllers you need to buy.

Unlike Joy-Con 2 sticks, the Nitro Deck 2 has full-sized thumbsticks, like the ones on the Pro Controller. They’re CaptiSticks which, like Hall Effect sticks, won't contract stick drift after using for a while. You can also adjust the resistance on them to your liking, and you can swap the stick tops and D-pad with the designs you like best (sold separately – see the alternates on CRKD ).

It also has four back buttons, two extra shoulder buttons, and fully re-mappable controls to give you more gameplay options than a standard controller. And thanks to a tightening dial on the back of the device, it’s also fully compatible with the original Switch and Switch OLED, which is a fun bonus if you still have one of those lying around.

What makes the default Switch 2 Joy-Cons so bad? Let me count the ways. The thumbsticks are too short for comfort. The grips are too thin, giving your hands little to hold onto. The face buttons are tiny. Playing a game using a single Joy-Con turned on its side feels terrible, but using two Joy-Cons also feel awkward and flat when snapped into a grip. To me, they basically feel awkward to use all the time.

Granted, these issues all arise as a result of Nintendo making the Joy-Cons 2 as versatile as possible. And to Nintendo's credit, they really can be used in a whole bunch of ways, some of which come in handy in certain situations. But when you make a controller a jack of all trades, it becomes a master of none. The ways I use my Switch 2 most – in handheld mode or in docked mode – the Joy-Cons just don't cut it.

If you ask me, the best thing to do with your default Joy-Cons 2 is to chuck them in the garbage and replace them with something else – like a Nitro Deck 2, perhaps?

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: Worms: The Board Game Is on Sale for Its Lowest Price Ever at Amazon
articles.body:
You're likely already familiar with the Worms video game series . It's a traditionally multiplayer game where you take your worms to all-out war with your opponent. There's bazookas, there's bombs, and there's almost always a whole lot of mayhem. Taking all of that chaos and bringing it to the tabletop may seem impossible, but it has in fact been done before.

Worms: The Board Game was first released back in 2024 by Mantic Games . It's normally available for around $40, but Amazon has dropped the price down to $25.97 for the first time ever.

The Worms board game is pretty straightforward, making it a solid option for beginners . You can play with up to four players, each of which will control their own team of four worms. Over about 45 minutes of playtime, you will battle each other to the death, blasting each other and the battlefield apart in true Worms fashion. Once one of the player's team of worms has been completely eliminated, the game ends, and the person with the most worms left is declared the winner.

Worms: The Board game may not be one of the best board games we've reviewed over the last few years, but it's still a fun way to kill some time (and worms) with friends. If you're looking for a tabletop experience that doesn't take itself too seriously, it's definitely worth picking up at this price.

articles.title: Microsoft's Special Edition Translucent Green Xbox Series X Pricing Details Have Leaked, and It's Just as Costly as We'd Feared
articles.summary: Pricing details for Microsoft's special edition 25th anniversary Xbox Series X have leaked online — and the translucent green console is just as expensive as we'd feared.
articles.body:
Pricing details for Microsoft's special edition 25th anniversary Xbox Series X have leaked online — and the translucent green console is just as expensive as we'd feared.

The ever-reliable billbil-kun from Dealabs has now revealed that the console will cost an eye-watering €899.99, which typically translates to the same $899.99 price point in the U.S.

A release date has also been uncovered: November 27, which lines up neatly with Black Friday. Notably, however, this is later than the October 20 launch date previously leaked for the 25th anniversary Xbox Series X controller . (You'll also get one with the console, of course, but these will also be available separately.)

While €899.99 may sound like a lot (and it is), it's worth putting in some context. After various price rises, this is now just €100 more than the standard Xbox Series X with a disc drive, and the same price as a standard PlayStation 5 Pro. It is also a price that may still tempt many OG fans, due to the console's stylish design — reminiscent of the original Xbox console launched a quarter of a century ago.

There's no getting around the fact that consoles are simply getting more expensive, as manufacturers deal with tariff and logistical uncertainties, plus spiralling memory costs due to the rise of AI data centers. Just yesterday, Nintendo confirmed the new U.K. pricing for Switch 2 , which will rise in cost within the U.S. and Europe from September 1.

Microsoft is expected to make its special edition 25th anniversary Xbox Series X pricing and availability official next week at Gamescom. Stand by for official confirmation then, and much more from the show here on IGN.

articles.title: What to Expect from ONL | gamescom 2026
articles.summary: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past and Final Fantasy 7 Revelation will be at gamescom Opening Night Live, but what surprises could be in store? Here's what to expect from ONL on August 25.
articles.body:
It’s that time of year when it's fun to just wildly speculate (and make some educated deductions) about what we might see from Geoff Keighley’s Opening Night Live, direct from gamescom 2026. Little is known ahead of time this year – a few games and studios have been teased, but for the most part the show is a complete mystery, and so this gives me plenty of room to dream about what surprises the show may have in store.

Taking place on August 25 at 11am PT/2pm ET/8pm CEST, here’s how to watch the stream . Let’s not waste any more time, though, and get straight into what to expect from it.

It’s going to be a big night for a couple of the most popular RPGs to ever exist. We’re officially getting our first look at The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt – Songs of the Past , the third expansion to Geralt’s landmark adventure, coming a whole 12 years after the base game’s release. Co-developed by CD Projekt Red and Fool’s Theory, it’s being described as a prologue of sorts to the upcoming The Witcher 4. Soon, the mystery behind the new, third sword Geralt is holding in the artwork may be revealed, as well as plenty more fans are eager to learn all about, including the expansion’s location and when in The Witcher timeline Songs of the Past is set.

Speaking of old games being revisited, we’ll be getting another look at Final Fantasy 7 Revelation , the last part of Square Enix’s remake trilogy. The project’s director, Naoki Hamaguchi, will be in attendance to show us what’s next for Cloud and the gang, but what exactly could we see? June’s SGF gave us a healthy dose of Highwind action, showing off how we’ll be able to skydive from the iconic airship down to any part of the open world we choose, as well as glimpses into how new party members Vincent Valentine and Cid will control in combat. So, what’s next? Perhaps a deeper dive into one or both of those characters, or maybe a more story-focused sneak peek?

We do know that story is exactly what we’ll be seeing more of from Gears of War: E-Day , though. A brand new trailer for the prequel will be shown at ONL, which will, presumably, include Marcus Fenix slicing up some Locusts. Game of Thrones: War for Westeros will have its gameplay reveal trailer shown off, too. The real-time strategy game puts you in control of one of the fantasy series’ major forces, from the Starks to the Night King’s White Walkers, as you attempt to rewrite Westeros history.

Other games confirmed for the show include Ananta, an upcoming free-to-play open-world game from NetEase that looks to be incorporating all sorts of action into its futuristic city setting. It certainly looks very ambitious, and we’re keen to see more, including, hopefully, a reveal of its release date. Then there’s Ontos, a new sci-fi horror game from Soma and Amnesia studio, Frictional Games. Starring Stellan Skarsgård as one of the occupants of its creepy lunar hotel called Samsara, we’re intrigued to find out more. Action RPG Showa American Story is also set to show up, with a new look at the game that places you in the shoes of a stuntwoman exploring a post-apocalyptic United States. It will be joined by Stage Tour , the rhythm game aiming to pick up where Guitar Hero and Rock Band left off. Then there’s Mewgenics, for which a musical performance is planned on stage. Could some sort of announcement be made for the cat-based tactics game? DLC or a console release, maybe?

The most recent confirmations to be present at the show include Metro 2039 , which, somehow looks like the shooter series’ darkest chapter yet. With it supposedly coming early next year, a good look at gameplay would be welcomed. Also, we know that Tides of Annihilation will be there, presumably with more of that slick-looking combat to show off.

Now for the fun part. What reveals and surprises may await us at ONL? Well, there are a whole host of games coming in September that would presumably love to stand out in the crowd. A big stage like this is the perfect opportunity. These include Marvel’s Wolverine, Control Resonant, Silent Hill: Townfall, Onimusha: Way of the Sword, The Blood of Dawnwalker , and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave , to name but a few. New trailers for all of these are distinct possibilities.

Moving into October, Call of Duty has somewhat of a tradition of turning up at gamescom to show off a slice of action. Modern Warfare 4 is this year’s offering from Infinity Ward, and is currently available to play in beta. Also due in October is Phantom Blade Zero . We did just get a chunky look at it at the recent State of Play, but we wouldn’t be surprised to see even more of its flashy sword combat here.

Looking beyond this year, Fable is set to be one of 2027’s biggest games, and we’d love another look at Playground Games’ reboot. Even more gameplay would be a treat, especially an insight into the RPG’s combat. We’ve seen a lot of the world and the people living it; now, let’s see how we can kill them.

What other games would you like to see pop up? Perhaps God of War Laufey ? Exodus ? If you’re feeling particularly ambitious, perhaps Persona 6 or the Ocarina of Time remake ? And no, there won’t be any GTA 6. That’s two days later on Netflix.

Let us know in the comments about what you’re most excited about at gamescom’s Opening Night Live show, taking place on August 25, 2026 at 11am PT/2pm ET/8pm CEST.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer Delivers a Blood-Drenched Comic Book Epic
articles.summary: The wildly popular action-horror comic Exquisite Corpses is getting a new spinoff focused on the Fox Mask Killer, and we've got a blood-drenched new preview of all the gory fun.
articles.body:
As far as horror comics go, Exquisite Corpses certainly boasts a novel format. Technically, the series is created by James Tynion IV and Michael Walsh, but in the spirit of the exquisite corpse concept, each issue shifts to a new creative team, who tell a story about one of the stylish killers in this action-horror universe. And sometimes, these new stories are so good they just demand a spinoff. That's where Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer comes in.

IGN can exclusively debut a new preview of Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer #1. Check out the slideshow gallery below to see three brand-new interior pages and the previously revealed cover art, but beware of some violent imagery ahead:

Exquisite Corpses: Fox Killer #1 Preview Gallery

As mentioned, Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer is a spinoff of the main series, reuniting writer Che Grayson (Absolute Catwoman), artist Adam Gorham (Infernal Hulk), and colorist Jordie Bellaire (Wonder Woman) as they delve much deeper into the hyperviolent world of the titular masked assassin. Like Exquisite Corpses, Fox Mask Killer is published through Tynion's Tiny Onion imprint and Image Comics.

Here's Tiny Onion's official summary of the new series:

Among killers-for-hire, there are a select few feared even among other assassins. The enigmatic Fox Mask Killer is at the top of that list. But now she wants the one thing even she can’t have – she wants out. And the only person who can offer her an opportunity to get away from her old life may be the devil herself…Discover the thrilling – and tragic – backstory of Exquisite Corpses’ most emblematic killer.

“From the moment James and Michael welcomed me into the world of Exquisite Corpses, I knew it was something special,” said Grayson in a statement. “I gravitated instantly to Fox Mask Killer, a character whose design alone provoked a rich backstory and undeniable aura. The biggest treat for me as a writer was the challenge of bringing depth to a character whose face readers would never see…until now. With this new limited series, the mask finally comes off, and I couldn’t be more excited to team up again with my best mate Adam alongside stellar talents Jordie and Becca. This is a dream project for me and I think fans of Fox Mask Killer and the Exquisite Corpses series are going to be very happy with the high stakes and even higher emotions thrill ride we have her on.”

Exquisite Corpses: Fox Mask Killer #1 will be released on September 16, with a final order cutoff of August 24. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop .

Previously, Tiny Onion expanded the series through an Exquisite Corpses card game . That game has now been successfully funded on Kickstarter.

For mroe, learn all about the new symbiote hero known as The Amazing Venom and see what to expect from Kevin Smith's epic Star Wars/Marvel crossover .

articles.title: Duchess of Sussex Meghan Markle is Reportedly Getting Back Into Acting
articles.summary: Meghan Markle, The Duchess of Sussex, is reportedly eyeing a return to acting.
articles.body:
UPDATE: Deadline has reported that Markle has had preliminary conversations to join Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen, should it be renewed for a third season.

ORIGINAL STORY: Meghan Markle, The Duchess of Sussex, is reportedly eyeing a return to acting.

After a lengthy break from performing — ever since her 2018 marriage to the U.K.'s Prince Harry — Markle has reportedly now been "offered a role in an upcoming project based in the U.K.," according to News.com.au . No further information about the role or production has been made public.

The timing of this news is interesting, as it comes just days after it was widely reported that both Harry and Meghan would soon move back to the U.K. for an extended period after six years living in California. During that time, Markle made appearances in various documentary and lifestyle series, though refrained from taking on fresh acting roles.

The British Royal Family in Movies and TV

Markle began her career with guest spots in TV series such as Knight Rider, Fringe, 90210, and CSI: Miami, before her breakthough role as Rachel Zane in legal drama Suits, a character she played between 2011 to 2018. It was during this time that she met Prince Harry, and the two subsequently married.

Markle's time as a working member of the Royal Family saw her focus on official duties with Harry rather than her acting roles. But Markle has so far failed to return to her former profession even after the couple's high-profile decision to step back from royal life and live in the U.S.

There has been no suggestion that Harry and Meghan's return to the U.K. will include a return to royal duties, and the couple will live in a private residence. The move follows a rare visit in July to see Harry's father, King Charles III. A BBC News report into this latest development includes mention of a royal source that stated they understood "the King was unaware of the move before last weekend, but he welcomes the opportunity to see more of the Sussex family in a private and personal capacity."

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine: 6 Comics to Read to Prepare for the Game
articles.summary: If you're impatiently waiting for the release of Marvel's Wolverine on the PS5, these six essential X-Men comics will help you prepare.
articles.body:
Marvel’s Wolverine may well be the most hotly anticipated game release of 2026 that isn’t GTA VI. After three excellent Spider-Man games from Insomniac, we’re finally getting the chance to pop some adamantium claws and slice and dice our way through endless hordes of robots, mercenaries, and ninja warriors.

One thing that’s become clear as more trailers and gameplay footage have been revealed is that Marvel’s Wolverine is taking a somewhat nontraditional approach to the X-Men franchise. For one thing, the game is set in a world where the X-Men themselves don’t yet exist. Even so, there are lots of familiar faces appearing in the game, and plenty of signs that Insomniac is looking closely to the comic book source material for help in crafting their storyline.

With that in mind, we’re taking a closer look at six classic Wolverine and X-Men comics you can read to help prepare you for the game. By the end, you’ll know everything you need to know about the most iconic X-Man of them all.

Marvel’s Wolverine is very pointedly about exploring Logan’s adventures as a solo hero, one who stalks the streets and seedy back alleys and finds trouble around every turn. There’s one comic that really set the tone for Wolverine as a solo hero and adventurer - the original 1982 Wolverine miniseries from Chris Claremont and Frank Miller.

Many fans would argue this is still the greatest Wolverine story ever published. It’s certainly the most influential, laying out a strong blueprint for Wolverine as a solo hero that many creators still follow to this day. The series brings Logan back to his old stomping grounds of Japan, where he strikes up a romance with the fair Lady Mariko, feuds with her oppressive father, Lord Shingen, and first encounters his ninja ally Yukio.

If you only read one Wolverine comic leading into the game, it should probably be this one. It’s a haunting and visually stunning look at a hardened killer trying to prove there’s more than meets the eye.

One of the interesting quirks of the new game is the fact that Sabretooth plays a supporting role. At this early stage in Wolverine’s costumed career, he and Sabretooth are still allies, though we have serious doubts as to whether that friendship will survive through the end of the story mode. It’s almost a guarantee that Logan and Victor Creed will eventually be at each other’s throats. That’s just how their relationship is.

There have been and continue to be a lot of great comics focused on the never-ending rivalry between these two men. But if we were to pick just one, we have to go with 1989’s Wolverine Vol. 2 #10, by Claremont and John Buscema.

This iconic tale introduces the notion that Sabretooth makes a point of hunting down Wolverine each year on the latter’s birthday to deliver a sadistic “present.” As the story jumps between past and present, readers get a full appreciation for just how deep this rivalry goes, and how much Logan has suffered over the years because of it.

The X-Men may not exist yet in the world of Marvel’s Wolverine, but that doesn’t mean Logan isn’t a team player. The game focuses instead on his history with the black ops group known as Team X, with Logan finding himself reluctantly drawn back into the fold in response to a new wave of mutant kidnappings.

For a good primer on Team X, it’s best to go back to the story in which they were introduced. X-Men Vol. 2 #4-7 digs deep into Logan’s history with the team even as it marks the debut of Russian mutant super-soldier Omega Red (a villain we know has a part to play in the game). As an added bonus, these issues are illustrated by Jim Lee, so there’s plenty of great ‘90s superhero nostalgia to go around.

Wolverine and Jean Grey have a complicated history, to say the least. There’s an undeniable mutual attraction there, but as Logan himself plainly said once, “It would never work between us.”

That said, there are plenty of Logan/Jean shippers in the X-Men fandom, and they must be thrilled that the game is depicting an actual romance between the two characters. In this pre-X-Men team, presumably pre-Cyclops time period, Logan and Jean appear to be an item.

There have been many comics to explore the tense dynamic between the two (particularly in the wake of X-Men: The Animated Series), but perhaps the best place to look is 1995’s Weapon X miniseries. Part of the larger Age of Apocalypse crossover, Weapon X is set in an alternate timeline where En Sabah Nur rules North America and Wolverine frees Jean Grey from Mister Sinister’s slave pits. It’s a fascinating look at both characters and the bond they share. And while you’re at it, you might as well read the rest of the crossover. It’s still one of the best X-Men storylines of all time .

As seen in: Uncanny X-Men Vol. 1 #141-142

All signs point to the idea that Marvel’s Wolverine deals heavily with the mutant-hunting robots known as Sentinels. The trailers show Logan dealing with numerous agents of Sentinel creator Bolivar Trask, and the game looks to feature at least one boss battle with a massive robot.

To read up on the Sentinels and the threat they pose, one need look no further than the quintessential Sentinel storyline, “Days of Future Past.” “Days of Future Past” introduces a bleak future where the Sentinels have risen up and killed or enslaved most of mutantkind. Only an aged Wolverine, Kate Pryde, and a handful of other heroes remain to mount a resistance. And the key to that resistance is sending Kate back in time to stop the assassination of Senator Robert Kelly.

Though only two issues long, this story has had a profound effect on the X-Men franchise and has been adapted several times in other media, including the 2014 movie of the same name .

As seen in: House of X #1-6 & Powers of X #1-6

The trailers for Marvel’s Wolverine also suggest that Mister Sinister has a key role in the game, with allusions to Sinister’s human guise of Nathaniel Essex. In fact, we wouldn’t be surprised if this twisted mad scientist winds up being the game’s main villain. It’s definitely worth reading up on Sinister before diving into Insomniac’s latest.

Here, again, there’s no shortage of options for good source material. That said, we’d lean towards the twin miniseries House of X and Powers of X from 2019. Sinister is a key figure in these tales, particularly the latter, as it explores the possible futures of the Marvel Universe 10, 100, and 1000 years down the line. House of X and Powers of X profoundly reshaped the direction of the X-Men line for years to come.

One of the things we love about these two books is that they crystallized the modern characterization of Sinister. No longer the straightforwardly evil mastermind of the X-Men franchise, House of X and Powers of X give him a much campier and more demented personality that helps him stand out all the more. We can only hope Insomniac was looking to these comics when it came to depicting Sinister in the game.

articles.title: This Awesome LEGO-Like Original Xbox Building Kit Is Still Available to Preorder (But It's Sold Out at Amazon)
articles.summary: Mattel has announced a LEGO-like building kit for the original Xbox game console in celebration of its 25th anniversary, but it's selling out fast.
articles.body:
In celebration of Xbox’s 25th anniversary, Mattel Brick Shop has announced a new LEGO-like building kit for a display model of Microsoft’s original Xbox game console. Once assembled, this 3,509-piece set turns into a 1:1 scale model of the device. It includes the console, a hefty full-size Duke controller, and hidden dioramas for three major Xbox games. It looks great, and it’s available for preorder now ( see it at Best Buy ), with a price tag of $329.99 and a release date of October 1 . However, it has already sold out at Amazon , so you may want to buy it sooner than later if you're interested.

Mattel Brick Shop - Microsoft Original Xbox

The console itself looks pretty much just like an original Xbox from 2001. Like like the LEGO Game Boy , the hefty Duke controller has buttons you can press – and when you press them, it triggers interactive lights and sounds in the dioramas hidden inside the console. According to the press release, “Fans can also discover a hidden button combination that triggers an exclusive lighting sequence.” Pretty cool.

The dioramas are worth calling out specifically. Tucked under panels in the console itself are little scenes from three popular Xbox games: Halo: Combat Evolved , The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind , and Psychonauts . (Yes, it's ironic that this is coming out after Microsoft has spun off Psychonauts developer Double Fine Productions). You can keep the dioramas hidden, or you can remove them to display alongside the set.

Additionally, the set comes with 12 “NanoWorld” figures from the games, including Halo’s Master Chief, Psychonauts’ Razputin Aquato, and more.

Formerly known as Mega Bloks, Mattel Brick Shop launched in 2025 as a line of buildable models that come in pieces for you to put together. If that sounds familiar, yes, they’re very similar to LEGO sets . But if the world is big enough for both Coke and Pepsi to co-exist, why not two competing lines of buildable models?

One difference between the two companies is that they’ve courted different brand licenses. LEGO has the likes of Nintendo , Pokémon , Star Wars , and Harry Potter . Mattel, the newer of the two lines, has Masters of the Universe , Hot Wheels , and Xbox. If you’re interested, you can find more Mattel Brick Shop sets here .

articles.title: A Classic Scene From the I Spy Books Has Been Recreated in LEGO
articles.body:
The I Spy book series is a favorite of mine. I collected all of the books as a kid (including the challenge ones!) and have recently started looking at them with my son again. The attention of detail that went into creating each scene is quite incredible and you can always find new things if you look hard enough.

As impressive as the creation of these scenes are, what's even more impressive is that someone has gone ahead and recreated it with only LEGO bricks. Posted in the LEGO Reddit this morning, user burnt-coding shared an image of the scene called "Blocks" from the very first I Spy book.

I recreated an I SPY scene with Lego by u/burnt-coding in lego

Seeing as I own this book myself, I decided to do my own thorough comparison of Walter Wick's original design compared to this brick-built version. And honestly, it's really quite impressively done. The main things that the builder wasn't able to accurately portray were the 11 bears. As indicated in the post, they had to replace the bears with helmets to be able to get close. There's also the three-headed dragon, which seems to have been replaced by three parrots instead. The minifigures don't exactly align with the original figures in the book, but they do get close.

All-in-all, it's a really impressive feat that requires pieces from a ton of different builds. I even recognized the cow and horse figures featured here from LEGO's Duplo Farm set that I recently purchased for my son. This is a MOC that resonates deeply with one of my favorite childhood activities and one of the reasons I love keeping up with the LEGO community. This is the kind of set I would happily buy if it ever got turned into a LEGO Ideas set .

Can You Still Buy the Original I Spy Book?

If you don't still own a copy of the original I Spy book, the good news is that you can still buy the hardcover version on Amazon. It's not the exact same edition I own, but the only difference seems to be slight changes to the cover art. The "Blocks" scene is the first picture riddle featured in this book, and parts of it are also featured in various Challenge books I Spy later released.

articles.title: A $200 Movie Made by a Chinese Mother and Her Son Just Beat Obsession to Become the World's Most Profitable Film  After Making 20,000 Times Its Budget
articles.summary: Low-budget Chinese animated film Niu Lai has just become the most profitable movie relative to its budget, beating out Obsession’s previous record in a baffling turn of events.
articles.body:
Low-budget Chinese animated film Niu Lai has just become the most profitable movie ever relative to its budget, beating out Obsession’s previous record in a baffling turn of events.

If you haven’t heard of Niu Lai, don’t worry — it’s a roughly-animated CGI movie that released exclusively in Chinese theaters on August 5 with little to no fanfare. Despite barely having any sort of promotional campaign, it soared at the Chinese box office, raking in RMB 29 million ($4.3 million USD) during its theatrical run.

That’s a pretty impressive number, considering the type of film Niu Lai is. It boasts extremely rough graphics and was reportedly created on a budget of just $200 , making its eye-watering profits a massive achievement.

During its first 10 days in theaters, the movie only brought in RMB 7,700 ($1,145 USD), with fewer than 300 tickets sold. It wasn’t long before footage and screenshots from the film started surfacing online, prompting morbidly curious viewers to flock to cinemas to see it for themselves, resulting in a hilarious cultural moment that skyrocketed Niu Lai to national, and now international, fame. Theater employees even made their own promotional posters by hand, as there was simply no marketing budget to advertise it.

So, what is Niu Lai about? The film follows a newborn calf named Niu Lai who learns to overcome his fears in an “abstract” dream sequence. It was created by a mother-son duo, Xin Yumeng and Sun Lifang, who spent five years creating it mostly by themselves.

Earning over $4 million on a project made on a mere $200 budget is nothing to sneeze at, and it means that this unexpected film toppled one of the most highly-lauded flicks of the summer: Obsession, which famously became the most world's profitable movie in history relative to its cost on a budget of less than $1 million .

With almost no marketing budget but plenty of unexpected hype, Niu Lai has cinemas across China making their own promotional posters by hand. Theater staff are putting their finest artistic skills to work. https://t.co/u2rpHlNUDb pic.twitter.com/mbeHJm4T8W — Shanghai Daily (@shanghaidaily) August 18, 2026

With almost no marketing budget but plenty of unexpected hype, Niu Lai has cinemas across China making their own promotional posters by hand. Theater staff are putting their finest artistic skills to work. https://t.co/u2rpHlNUDb pic.twitter.com/mbeHJm4T8W

Niu Lai has since surpassed that record, drawing eyes internationally as it continues to gain traction online. While it’s become a world-famous meme of sorts, it’s unclear if its fame will translate to cinema showings outside of China, though there are certainly no shortage of curious commenters wanting to see it for themselves.

It’s been a big summer at the movies on just about all sides, with The Odyssey recently surpassing Deadpool & Wolverine to become the highest-grossing R-rated film of all time and Spider-Man: Brand New Day swinging past Avengers: Endgame’s record to become the fastest movie to reach $700 million at the domestic box office.

articles.title: Want a Gears of War Lancer Replica? You Can Preorder One Now
articles.summary: Preorders are live for a full-scale 1:1 Gears of War Prototype Lancer replica, but it'll set you back $300.
articles.body:
I think it’s safe to say that, ever since the original Gears of War hit the Xbox 360 back in 2006, many fans have wanted a lancer of their own. Now that Gears of War E-Day is coming soon, you can have one. An official Gears of War Prototype Lancer Replica is available for preorder on the Xbox Game Studios Shop . It’s not cheap at $299.99, but it’s a full-sized 1:1 scale model, and it looks terrific. Orders placed now are expected to ship in February 2027.

The iconic firearm is an assault rifle that has a chainsaw attached to it, or a “chainsaw bayonet,” if you want to sound elegant. Gears of War E-Day is a prequel to the Gears of War series, depicting the initial alien attack on the planet Sera. As a result, the Lancers used in the game are prototypes of the ones in later installments. Hence the word “prototype” in the name of the replica.

Now this isn’t the first Lancer replica to be released. In fact, we got to go hands-on with one a decade ago around the release of Gears of War 4. But this is the latest one, and it matches the weapons seen in Gears of War E-Day, complete with “a custom, hand-painted battle-worn ‘E-Day' finish that reflects the immediate chaos of the initial strike.”

The replica is full-scale and detailed, and it can be wielded to scare your friends, just like the real thing. But it’s intended to be a display piece, and as such, it comes with a stand and an informational placard so you can set it on your desk or shelf.

Gears of War E-Day comes out October 6, and preorders are live now . You can get a peek at the multiplayer in our first preview of the game.

articles.body:
The 4K Blu-ray releases for Toy Story 5 went up for preorder this morning. While the previously announced limited edition 4K steelbook seemed to have quickly sold out across retailers, it just came back in stock exclusively at Amazon . A standard Blu-ray and DVD are also still up for preorder with the same release date of September 22.

Toy Story 5's Limited Edition 4K Steelbook

It's not too hard to see why this particular steelbook got snapped up so fast. The cover art is pretty top of the line, and celebrates Toy Story as a whole instead of being too specific to the new sequel.

Toy Story 5 - Limited-Edition 4K Steelbook

All of the artwork is in a unique watercolor style, with the main Toy Story trio as well as some of the new character additions on the front. On the back you'll see a certain emotionally devastating tire swing tree from Toy Story 2 that makes its return in the new sequel.

Aside from being so darn pretty, the other reason this steelbook is in such high demand is because there doesn’t appear to be any standard 4K UHD release. In other words, anyone who was looking to grab the movie in 4K UHD was forced into the steelbook option.

Standard Blu-ray and DVD Also Still Available

The standard DVD and Blu-ray are still available at multiple retailers. These feature the same cover art that matches the primary Toy Story 5 poster, showing the team of familiar toys gawking in fear at the sequel's new villain, LilyPad.

The original press release also claimed there would be a new collected set of all five Toy Story movies, but no listings have popped up for that one yet.

Toy Story 5 was originally released in theaters back in June, where it grossed just over $1.1 billion worldwide. IGN’s own review claims it "manages to pull off an adventurous and resonant conclusion," though we had a couple thoughts about Woody’s involvement in the whole thing . articles.body:
An eagle-eyed fan spotted an extremely specific location from Cyberpunk 2077 in the new trailer for Edgerunners 2, earning praise from the show's official social media accounts as theories abound online.

Netflix dropped a new trailer and images for Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 on Thursday, giving us a closer look at Weak Kingsley, D, Roman Carax, and Talia Yang.

In the trailer’s opening shot, we see Night City’s skyline through a puddle. It’s a tranquil image that gets marred after what appears to be Weak Kingsley’s robotic arm — clearly damaged from some sort of scuffle — falls into it, while Kingsley (played by the iconic Clancy Brown) grunts in pain.

It didn’t take long for dedicated Cyberpunk fans to pinpoint the exact location of this puddle in the game itself, which they tracked down to a puddle right outside the Afterlife, a bar frequented by Johnny Silverhand and owned by legendary fixer Rogue Amendiares.

Their skills would give Rainbolt a run for his money, and even earned kudos from the official Cyberpunk: Edgerunners X account, who replied to their post: “You know Night City like the palm of your hand, choom.”

Still others can’t help but pick apart the data shard that D slots into his neck, which looks distinctly like a relic — an experimental data chip created by Arasaka intended to map out a person’s consciousness and imprint it onto the brain of another living person.

Relics are central to the plot of Cyberpunk 2077 . One of them was used to capture Johnny Silverhand’s mind, which was later imprinted onto the protagonist, V’s, brain, kicking off the rest of the game’s story.

articles.title: The Dungeon Crawler Carl TV Series Has Its Showrunners
articles.body:
The Dungeon Crawler Carl TV show has taken a big step forward with Chris Yost and Eric Heisserer being named co-showrunners for the series.

Matt Dinniman's popular LitRPG series was officially confirmed for Peacock earlier this year, but we haven't heard much news about it since then. Yost had already been attached to the project as writer, but the move to co-showrunner is a step up. The addition of Heisserer brings a second helping of sci-fi chops to the series.

Yost has worked on a number of Star Wars and Marvel projects over the years. He acted as a consultant and writer for the first season of The Mandalorian (which IGN gave an 8 out of 10 ) and co-wrote two Thor sequels (The Dark World and Ragnarok). He was also previously showrunner for the Paramount+ series Tales of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles .

Heisserer most recently worked as showrunner for Netflix's Shadow and Bone series, which he also created and produced. You may also recognize him as the writer of Denis Villeneuve's Arrival , which he adapted from Ted Chiang's popular sci-fi novella.

With seasoned sci-fi showrunners at the helm and Seth MacFarlane's Fuzzy Door involved, the Dungeon Crawler Carl series seems like it's being truly set up for success . During San Diego Comic-Con , it was also announced that the narrator of the audiobooks, Jeff Hays, would be reprising his role as the voice of Princess Donut. Dinniman himself praised the decision in an interview with IGN , saying, "He's so associated with that sound and that voice. Anybody else would be jarring."

While we still don't have any sort of release date attached to the series, the momentum created by the Dungeon Crawler Books themselves is likely to continue for years to come. Matt Dinniman still has two books left to write, and there's even a tabletop RPG based on the series releasing in December.

On the streaming side of things, Peacock recently announced its fourth price increase in four years. The increase arrives as the service is adding in YouTube Premium for its subscribers at no extra cost sometime in early 2027.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics -- from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: Genki’s New High-End PC and Switch 2 Controller Has a Built-in Screen and Onboard OS
articles.summary: Genki's new customizable controller has smashed its Kickstarter goal, packing in tons of high-end features like TMR sticks, adjustable triggers, and advanced haptics, as well as even more advanced tech like a full-blown operating system, complete with digital display, built into the controller itself.
articles.body:
Genki, maker of some of our favorite accessories for the Switch 2 and Switch , has launched a Kickstarter for what might be the most over-engineered controller I’ve ever seen – and for $279, it better be. The Genki Manta packs in the kind of cutting edge features found on the best controllers out there, like TMR sticks, adjustable triggers, and advanced haptics, as well as even more advanced tech like a full-blown operating system, complete with digital display, built into the controller itself.

Now, I’m all for hardware and peripherals that incorporate new tech and push their categories forward, but I’m not quite sure why anyone would need a controller this advanced. It’s undeniably well-designed – I appreciate the screen centered below the thumbsticks, instead of above like on the Turtle Beach Stealth Ultra , and how the tension of the thumbsticks can be dialed in (literally) on the fly by twisting the stick itself. But at some point you have to ask if we’re approaching the point of overkill.

Genki is taking a bit of a kitchen sink approach with the Mantra. “We refused to cut corners,” the Kickstarter reads. “It is, frankly, a spec monster.”

Compatible with PC via USB-C wired or 2.4 GHz wireless (via USB dongle) as well as Switch 1 and 2, mobile, and other devices via Bluetooth, the Manta has a standard Xbox-style layout with offset sticks and all your standard inputs. It has a 2,400 mAh user-replaceable battery, but there’s no mention on the Kickstarter page of an estimated usage time between charges. Blessedly, it can remotely wake a paired Switch 2.

The face buttons are “Analog Pulse Buttons” that track through their entire travel when pressed, not just when they bottom out, allowing users to adjust their actuation point anywhere between a quick rapid-reset for burst inputs and a deeper one that calls for a deliberate press. Similarly, the triggers have three distinct modes: Digital, which offers a short travel and crisp click, Rapid, which is fully analog but with a short, smooth travel, and Analog, which offers a full, smooth travel and proportional control.

Other features include “maglev haptics” (better than traditional rumble, apparently), a nine-axis gyroscope/accelerometer/compass for motion controls, six extra inputs (two buttons tucked up top next to the right and left bumpers, two integrated back buttons, and two removable back paddles), and a D-pad that can swap between a traditional cardinal layout and an eight-point satellite dish design.

And that’s not even mentioning the operating system built into the controller. MantaOS uses the controller’s built-in color display to handle all the configuration settings that would normally be handled by driver software or a companion app – stuff like swapping profiles, setting up macros, adjusting inputs, and customizing RGB lighting – right there on the controller.

But it does more than that too – and this is the part where, in the writing of this story, my thinking started to shift from “this is unnecessarily over-engineered” to “wait, that’s actually awesome.” There’s a small button next to the right thumbstick that pulls up an “On-the-Fly KBM” when pressed, turning the screen into a QWERTY or Compass Quick Type keyboard; or hold the button to turn the whole controller into a gyro-controlled mouse input. This is immensely useful for navigating the Windows desktop and bypassing login screens or game launchers. It’s the same sort of thing that makes the Steam Deck and Steam Machine more user-friendly than a handheld or PC running windows, except the solution is handled controller-side instead of by SteamOS.

MantaOS has some other neat tricks, like a macro action timeline that goes beyond recording a series of inputs and delays to fully tracking analog stick paths, trigger pressure, and more, meaning you can record a full gameplay sequence to repeat, such as a difficult boss runback (I’m looking at you, Bilewater ). The screen also has a variety of customizable dashboards to display stuff like your active profile, polling rate, battery, and connection status.

There’s even a programmable layer, running on a dual-core Raspberry Pi RP2350, that can load external apps onto the controller’s 16 MB of internal storage. The Kickstarter shows a clip of a side-scrolling space shooter playing on the built-in screen, and mentions the possibility of developing a “Genki Forge” for users to develop and share homebrewed apps for MantaOS. I have no doubt that someone will get Doom running on it in no time.

The Genki Manta Kickstarter is live now, and as of this writing has around 1,800 backers and more than $400,000 pledged – four times its $100,000 goal. The controller will eventually be priced at $279, but a Super Early Bird pledge tier drops the price down to $189, which puts it in conversation with other high-end controllers like the DualSense Edge . That’s still nearly double the excellent Steam Controller , which has its own set of unique tricks, but at $100 also lacks a great deal of the advanced tech found here.

Genki hopes to start shipping the Manta to backers this coming January, but conservatively estimates the delivery window to January through April 2027. We’ll be testing the Mantra as soon as we can go hands-on, so be sure to look out for our review as we get closer to that launch date.

Bo Moore is IGN's Senior Manager of Tech. You can find him online @usebomswisely.
