articles.title: IGN's Top Reviewed Movies of 2026 So Far
articles.summary: IGN has already reviewed quite a few movies in 2026, but only one film has earned a perfect 10 out of 10 (and it's not even out yet!).
articles.body:
IGN has already reviewed quite a few movies in 2026, but only one film has earned a perfect 10 out of 10 (and it's not even out yet!). If you're wondering which movies our reviewers have loved this year, we've gathered everything that's earned a score of 8 or above in one place.

We're pretty excited for some really big movies coming out in the latter half of the year, but in the meantime, you can check out our top picks as of August 2026. As a quick reminder, here's what each of these review scores means:

From our review : "The tragedy of an eight-year-old who witnesses a sexual assault, and who has to find her own strength when her parents fail to help her cope, Beth de Araújo’s Josephine is one of the year’s most aesthetically sure-footed films. Mason Reeves delivers one of the most stunning child performances in recent memory, while Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan lean into their familiar acting hallmarks but find uncomfortable new layers as a mother and father bound by their own upbringings. The result is visceral, gentle, and ultimately, shattering." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "Sam Raimi drives the survival thriller genre to some amazing and sadistically giddy ends, with Rachel McAdams and Dylan O’Brien along for the ride in the back seat cackling and stabbing each other the whole way through. Linda and Bradley’s ordeal creates immensely fertile ground for Raimi to interrogate the validity of first impressions with twists and turns of the plot and of various sharp objects that seldom tire. Sure, drag me to hell, but let's stop at this island on the way and have a freakin’ party with Linda and Bradley!" - Tom Jorgensen

From our review : "Harking back to their low-budget web series, Toronto comedians Matt Johnson and Jay McCaroll – who reprise their roles as indie musicians trying to score a major gig at any cost – inject mockumentary comedy with an incredible sci-fi twist in one of the year’s most daringly silly films. Part guerrilla prank saga, part heartwarming friendship story, and part riff on Back to the Future, the result is an incredibly fine-tuned mishmash of styles and ideas that keeps evolving in surprising ways." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "Baz Luhrmann delivers a thrilling big-screen tribute to Elvis Presley with EPiC. Presley’s humanity and energy pour off the screen, even if the subject himself – who “narrates” his own story – is circumspect in what personal details he’s willing to reveal. This is more a chronicle of Elvis the artist and performer than Elvis the man, although the high and low points of his life and career up until 1972 are covered. As an experience for Elvis fans – and if you’re not a fan, this film could likely make you one – EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert is unparalleled." - Jim Vejvoda

From our review : "The Drama is a practically absurd but emotionally true-to-life tale about the fears of being known, and being truly seen. Kristoffer Borgli imbues his bleakly comic stress-test of modern romance with a destabilizing cinematic energy, as a deep, dark, and very American secret threatens his characters’ domestic bliss by exposing the limits of their empathy. Led by immaculate performances, it’s one of the most delightfully nerve-wracking rabbit holes you’re likely to tumble down this year." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "Erupcja is not just the best Charli XCX film to date, but the best work yet from the poetic filmmaker Pete Ohs, with the two finding kindred spirits in each other. Though it could be wrongly dismissed as slight, look deeper into the well-crafted, wondrous portrait that the duo creates together, and you’ll find one of those films whose rich vibrancy sneaks up on you." - Chase Hutchinson

From our review : "A zesty, energetic biopic about a teenage Anthony Bourdain, Matt Johnson’s second film this year is an act of controlled chaos, tapping into the nostalgia of naïve youth while examining how creativity is born. Led by an incredible ensemble, its imperfect answers make for one of the finest and thorniest coming-of-age films in recent years. It’s a blast." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma is as much Jane Schoenbrun again at their best as it sees them taking us in surprising new directions. It’s sexual, sincere, silly, and sweet all at once – an earnest exploration of desire that’s deeply, movingly personal. For all the ways it could lose people in its messiness, Schhoenbrun and their strong cast hold it all together, building to an ecstatic climax that will only make you wish you could come back for more." - Chase Hutchinson

From our review : "After the largely disappointing Crisis trilogy, Batman: Knightfall Part 1 - Knightfall is a strong return to form for DC’s direct-to-video movie line. The first part of this animated trilogy succeeds in cutting through the fat and adapting the essential core of a classic Batman crossover. It paints a vivid psychological portrait of both Batman and his latest arch-nemesis. The film also looks great and boasts a talented voice cast that brings this venerable source material to life. This new DC animated trilogy is off to a great start." - Jesse Schedeen

From our review : "Coyote vs. Acme succeeds on just about every level, showing a clear understanding of what makes the classic Looney Tunes characters so timeless. It’s a savvy mix of absurd humor, a satirical, meta-subplot, and just enough emotional weight to make us care about these short-form animated punching bags for a full feature-length runtime. With capable leads in Will Forte, John Cena, and Lana Condor highlighted by hilarious bits from the supporting cast, Coyote vs. Acme proves the Looney Tunes won’t be going anywhere so long as they keep chasing that bird." - Clint Gage

From our review : "Through forests, mountainsides, and claustrophobic main streets, Hope launches a gonzo sensory assault with an action-comedy-thriller saga of a small town beset by forces much larger than itself. Beginning with a lengthy climax, then unspooling a mystery in reverse before climaxing once again, its peculiar structure is as uncannily inviting as its malformed creature designs, which work to bring cultural paranoia into a riveting clash with nature. It’s a nonstop blast with the kind of low-to-the-ground vehicular and horseback action that’ll have you falling off the front of your seat." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "A gruff, must-watch Ethan Hawke leads a delightful band of outsiders in The Weight, a Depression-era heist film that oscillates between slow burn drama and nail-biting intensity. Its tale of prisoners tasked with transporting stolen gold in exchange for their freedom is equal parts political leaflet and western folklore, resulting in a slick thriller that charges breathlessly forward." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "28 Years Later: The Bone Temple is getting an 8. Director Nia DaCosta crafts a great follow-up to last year’s 28 Years Later that’s gory and thoughtful in equal measure. There’s a wit and humor at play in The Bone Temple that elevates, in all the right ways, the dramatic stakes of a zombie apocalypse working on its third decade, especially in Ralph Fiennes’ record collection (I’d give the film a 666 if IGN would let me). While it might not be the best place to start watching the 28 Later franchise for the uninitiated, the creative force driving the series’ future have two solid movies as the foundation for whatever comes next." - Clint Gage

Read our review : "Spectacular visuals, imaginative worldbuilding, and topical themes elevate a broadly drawn plot in Mamoru Hosada’s very loose Hamlet adaptation. This animé epic from the Japanese auteur behind Mirai and Belle is worth seeing on a big screen." - Kayti Burt

From our review : "Goat tells a basic and familiar underdog sports story, but in a warm-hearted and endearing manner, with likable characters you can easily root for, even if adults in the audience can easily predict how things will play out for them. And it really soars on the animation front, with some especially clever and dynamic visuals that help make the centerpiece games really special, and allow this world of anthropomorphic animals to feel unique, even with plenty of competition on that front." - Eric Goldman

From our review : "Thrilling, heartfelt, and hilarious, Project Hail Mary is a rollicking sci-fi blockbuster. Lord and Miller faithfully adapt Andy Weir’s novel, carrying forward the author’s celebration of science, teamwork, and bravery on a huge scale, bolstered by great performances from Ryan Gosling and James Ortiz and Greig Fraser’s fantastic work behind the camera. Some pacing issues inherent in closely adapting the novel’s structure do make for a somewhat rough landing, but through the lens of Grace and Rocky’s partnership being the real mission we want to see succeed, Project Hail Mary is a memorable celebration of how much we can accomplish when we work together." - Tom Jorgensen

From our review : "They Will Kill You is another winner from director Kirill Sokolov that shows Zazie Beetz has all the chops to be an action star in her own right. With great stunt choreography and camerawork, it’s a shining example of how modern action ought to be constructed. With a supernatural, satanic twist that it fully capitalizes on, it’s a gonzo, gruesome, gutsy little gem." - Chase Hutchinson

From our review : "The question of how and why you would even attempt to remake Faces of Death is given a compelling answer in this new remake. Using a postmodern meta take on both the original film and how it was perceived, the movie reflects a world where rather than hunting down a specific VHS tape to see people supposedly really die, you can now find exactly that type of content immediately by simply going on the internet…and that is far from a comforting thought!" - Eric Goldman

From our review : "In Steven Soderbergh’s deceptively simple The Chistophers, Ian McKellen delivers a blistering, abrasive performance as an aging artist fighting the tides of change, while being gradually conned by Michaela Coel as a beguiling art student who hopes to forge his unfinished work. Part caper and part artistic self-reflection, the movie plays like a late-stage masterwork, but one that Soderbergh has arrived at decades early, leaving the door open to infinite possibilities." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "David Lowery’s latest is a visually fascinating chamber piece with great performances from Anne Hathaway and Michaela Coel. The story of old wounds between former friends and creative partners isn’t the most relatable mannequin on which to assemble a film, so the story of icon Mother Mary and couture designer Sam doesn’t have enough range to carry the film through its final moments. However, everything else, from the sound design to the cinematography and the operatic fantasy of this pop star ghost story (a subgenre I wouldn’t have pegged as “up my alley” but here we are) makes Mother Mary a great piece of art." - Clint Gage

From our review : "Baltasar Kormákur delivers a compelling survival thriller with both Charlize Theron and Taron Egerton throwing themselves into their adversarial roles. Theron crafts a relatable and grounded performance bolstered with emotional sensitivity and physical prowess, while Taron Egerton proves his worth as a weirdly menacing antagonist. Immersively conceived and nerve-rackingly realized, Apex is a visually-commanding action film bursting with impressively dynamic stunt sequences." - Hanna Ines Flit

From our review : "The Sheep Detectives is a very sweet, and often quite moving, family comedy about grief and death. I know that sounds weird, but director Kyle Balda and screenwriter Craig Mazin are mostly successful at threading that needle, with the broad humor of some of the human characters being the film’s weakest aspect. The sheep characters Lily and Sebastian have compelling arcs that highlight the movie’s themes of acceptance and growth. As dark as the story can sometimes get, there’s still enough warmth and wit to make The Sheep Detectives appropriate for younger audiences." - Jim Vejvoda

From our review : "Mortal Kombat II gets an 8 from me. It might not be Oscar-caliber cinema, and hardcore fans of the game with encyclopedic knowledge of the game may have a bone to pick, but it’s big and loud and gruesome and not afraid to have fun. The bar for video game movie sequels isn’t very high, but this one not only clears the bar, it twirls it around like a bo staff." - Max Scoville

From our review : "I Love Boosters, Boots Riley’s candy-colored indictment of capitalism, is as sharp as it is deranged. Living somewhere along the spectrum of magical realism, the entire film is a brilliant balancing act of comedy and call-to-action that sprinkles a little philosophy in-between. Expertly executed production, set, costume and prop design bring Riley’s unique vision to life, while just as vital are the performances of our ensemble, led by Keke Palmer. Her turn as Corvette is the earnest heartbeat of a delightfully insane film." - Alyssa Mora

From our review : "Pressure is quality dad content. War movie fans and WWII buffs should appreciate the film’s devotion to detail, while mainstream audiences will be treated to a taut, compelling story about the very real men behind the icons who ensured an Allied victory. Brendan Fraser makes Eisenhower flesh and blood, while Andrew Scott adds another whipsmart protagonist to his filmography with his nuanced portrayal of meteorologist James Stagg." - Jim Vejvoda

From our review : "Backrooms expertly expands on the conceptual groundwork of the YouTube series with smart visual composition, beautifully terrifying production design, a complex protagonist, and a return to Kane Parsons’ roots of computer generated sequences that pack a serious punch. The film also opens the doors to some compelling pathways to deepen the lore even more, if newcomers are willing to meet the film on its level, where it isn’t going to spoon-feed anyone. Parsons’ film is a harrowing trip to the dark heart of fractured memory, loneliness, and inner turmoil. It takes what’s psychologically horrifying about the liminality of life and transmogrifies it into something truly terrifying. That’s something the concept has always done well, and its future seems bright with Parsons at the helm of the nightmarish maze." - Lex Briscuso

From our review : "Obsession should and will put Barker on the map as a horror filmmaker you need to watch. Thanks to fantastic turns by Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, you'll be addicted to this sour Valentine's Day counterprogramming. The film plays on familiar romance and monkey's paw tropes, turning a wish against the wishee, but Barker's execution takes things to the next level. In the film's simplicity lay the chance to go for broke, putting all efforts into the lengths Nikki is willing to go for her beloved. With that focus and Barker's fearlessness, Obsession becomes one hell of a maximalist ride." - Matt Donato

From our review : "Masters of the Universe is so much funnier than I expected, and the fight scenes are choreographed and photographed in a way that gives the sequences just enough flair to make them stand out (even if they’re not revolutionizing superhero style fisticuffs on screen). While Nicholas Galitzine and Idris Elba provide the thematic structure to the film, Jared Leto’s Skeletor gives a delightfully weird and cartoonish energy to every scene he’s in. It’s a film that appreciates the source material, silly names and all, and proves the best way to add to a 50-year-old franchise that’s about toys as much as anything else is to not take it too seriously." - Clint Gage

From our review : "The story of a small-town girl falling for a career criminal and going on a cross-country crime spree with him is one we’ve certainly seen before, but Carolina Caroline provides its own spin on the subject that makes it well worth checking out. Samara Weaving and Kyle Gallner have long proven themselves as actors whose presence always enlivens any movie they’re in. Here, they’re excellent together in a movie that does a great job of selling you on the genuine emotion behind its scenario rather than pushing it to over-the-top extremes." - Eric Goldman

From our review : "In a just world, The Furious will be an unprecedented hit for Lionsgate Films; not only is it worthy, but it's an antidote to the formulaic action movies Hollywood likes to churn out. Tanigaki brings electric energy and crowd-pleasing visuals to a rough-and-tumble ready-to-rumble actioner that walks the walk over and over. It's a winning formula: the stuntman director, a cast of world-class martial artists, and an unlimited tank of adrenaline. It’s another instant addition to my collection of international genre favorites, and one I'll be revisiting whenever I need a healthy excitement boost." - Matt Donato

From our review : "Adrian Chiarella’s Leviticus is an involving, meaningful, and legitimately creepy horror movie. Chiarella’s story about gay youth being punished for simply being the way they are is emotional and thoughtful while also simply working well as a horror story, blending the real-life prejudices that inspired it with the supernatural curse laid upon its characters in a highly effective manner." - Eric Goldman

From our review : "When you have a franchise as successful as Despicable Me/Minions, why not have some fun with it and push the boundaries? That seems to have been the approach with Minions & Monsters, and it pays off. Using the Minions to create an ode to early Hollywood that’s also an overall love letter to movies themselves and the power of storytelling is a surprising yet welcome turn of events. The film manages to incorporate the usual type of Minions gags to please their many loyal fans (most importantly kids) while also interjecting references and story elements that have a lot of extra entertainment value for older viewers. And look, if even a handful of people of any age end up using the seventh movie in the Despicable Me franchise as a springboard to learn more about the likes of Buster Keaton or Orson Welles, that’s a net positive." - Eric Goldman

From our review : "Despite its noncommittal destination, The Invite makes for a nerve-racking journey for much of its runtime. With fine-tuned performances at her disposal, including her own, Wilde reclaims the title of director with ferocity and vigor, carving a stylized piece of cinema from a story that could’ve so easily been straightforward and simple in its telling. Instead, it becomes an entertaining mirror of romantic disillusionment in middle age and one of the more enjoyable adult dramas out of Hollywood this year." - Siddhant Adlakha

From our review : "Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is a must-watch cinematic experience, an epic film version of an epic poem that adapts many of the out-there concepts of Homer through a new eye that frequently brings a sense of horror and existential angst to the story – and even a bit of humor too! Matt Damon is fine as the title character if not revelatory, but the extensive supporting cast frequently prop up individual moments, as do some of Nolan’s unique additions to the story. While Odysseus’ emotional journey here can be as choppy as a rough day at sea, and the “civilization is eroding” theme is undercooked, the film’s bigger observations on the effects of war on those who are forced to participate in it are well met. The Odyssey isn’t perfect, but it’s a pretty great moviegoing experience all the same." - Scott Collura

From our review : "Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender is a lovingly crafted and gorgeously animated movie that features a welcome return for Team Avatar. While the plot might be a little thin, the action scenes and settings are thrilling and deserved to be seen on the big screen instead of streaming after a scuttled theatrical release and unfortunate leak changed plans that would have made this more of an event for fans." - Alex Zalben

From our review : "Refn's back on his business with Her Private Hell. At his best, he's one of the most exciting and visually exquisite filmmakers working in the industry today. Everything you expect from the whole-hog Refn experience is back with a vengeance, including his brand of airy, somewhat interpretive storytelling that's made titles like Only God Forgives and The Neon Demon so divisive. Her Private Hell is more of that, but in a way that's still exciting despite its charitable highs and befuddling lows. At the very least, it's splendid to look at throughout, and I don't mean that as a snide jab. Her Private Hell could be screenshotted and framed, and headline its own gallery takeover, while the story will leave some viewers dazed and confused: The Nicolas Winding Refn Special." - Matt Donato

From our review : "It Ends manages to be both creepy and amusing thanks to its likable cast and filmmaker Alexander Ullom’s ability to exploit minimal resources to maximum effect. This is a movie that takes place in a car. In the woods. That’s it! And yet it’s scary, the characters really grow on you, and it also poses some self-aware and probing questions that will at the very least have you putting on the Talking Heads’ album Little Creatures when you’re done." - Scott Collura

From our review : "With the brute force of director Casper Kelly’s impressive command of tone, Buddy overcomes some woefully inconsistent pacing to deliver a nightmarish, exciting deconstruction of children’s programming. Keegan-Michael Key does a good job supporting that tone through his bubbly-then-bearish performance, but Cristin Milioti and Delaney Quinn each steal the show as well-drawn characters who attack Buddy’s hold over them from different angles. Strong production design and original songs keep Buddy from feeling like it’s taking inspiration too liberally from any one source, and all that leaves Buddy standing on its own as a singular, satisfying horror-comedy." - Tom Jorgensen

Read our review : "The Only Living Pickpocket in New York is a tremendous sophomore feature from Mr. Segan, who's just as charming a filmmaker as he is an actor. There's a twinkly, winky nature about his ode to professions being left in the dust by contemporary society – even the underbelly ones. Turturro is a phenomenal actor, adding another classic turn to his already illustrious catalog. It's a melting pot of experiences from comical to romantic to thrilling to richly ruminative. Everything flows together gracefully in step through a delicate and beautiful dance that speaks to the ever-changing beast that is New York City. And, sometimes, you know the ride is over…when all you can do is reflect on how good you’ve had it." - Matt Donato

articles.title: The Best PC Gaming Collaboration Collections to Check Out Now
articles.summary: If you're a PC gamer with a passion for cool collabs, you won't want to overlook these killer crossovers.
articles.body:
Customization is king in this day and age, so gaming enthusiasts are always on the lookout for new and exciting ways to show off their favorite games, anime, movies, and more through their gaming gear. That's why it's nice to see so many collaborations, especially within the PC gaming space. With that in mind, we've gathered our picks for our favorite currently available collabs, so we feel confident you can find something that tickles your fancy below.

Secretlab Titan Evo Limited Edition Chairs

Secretlab Titan Evo Star Wars Stormtrooper XL

Secretlab is well-known for its top-tier gaming chairs, such as the Titan Evo , which comfortably ranks among the best gaming chairs of 2026 . With its best-in-class ergonomics and features, the Titan Evo has become a beloved choice for PC gamers looking for a premium seat. Additionally, the Titan Evo comes sporting a bevy of unique collaborations ranging from hit anime like Dragon Ball Z, Jujutsu Kaisen, and One Piece to popular games like Genshin Impact, Pokémon, Cyberpunk 2077, and League of Legends. And that's just grazing the surface; there are dozens of collabs available, so there's bound to be one that catches your eye.

Whether you're looking for the best pre-built gaming PCs or simply trying to find the perfect case for your own build, you want the final result to look snazzy in its environment. If you're looking for some truly spectacular collabs, Starforge's lineup of themed gaming PC cases may be right up your alley. These cases sport gorgeous UV-printed designs for anime like Chainsaw Man, Frieren, and Solo Leveling, all the way to unexpected gaming options like Terraria or Old School Runescape — and they all feature swappable acrylic platelights that help the inside of your build sell the theme, too. Whether you opt for a full pre-built or just the case, you can't go wrong with these stunners

Razer has been a mainstay in the PC gaming peripheral scene for decades, so it makes sense that the company would nail down some killer collabs. And one of its most sought-after includes the Razer Kraken Kitty V2 - Gengar Edition , which combines solid (albeit not entirely remarkable) audio and mic quality with the titular ghost Pokémon's purple aesthetic. It's a positively delightful option for Poké-fans, even if the $140 price tag feels like a bit unreasonable for a wired headset. But Razer went all in with more Gengar items, too, including themed versions of its Cobra mouse and Gigantus V2 XXL mousepad , so you can get a whole spooky set going if you're so inclined.

There's no denying the effect Genshin Impact has had in the world of gacha games, so it's no wonder it's the focal point of so many collaborations. One of the most impressive, however, comes from Logitech G , providing a full collection of peripherals celebrating the game. You can grab a Kamisato Ayaka-inspired G309 Lightspeed mouse , G515 Lightspeed TKL keyboard , and G733 Lightspeed headset . Meanwhile, the G305 Lightspeed mouse comes in special editions featuring character art for Sayu, Thoma, or Shikanoin Heizou.

There are plenty of unique gaming-specific collaborations on the market, but we just can't help but get a kick out of SteelSeries' South Park collection . It's most fitting that the QcK L micro-woven mousepad is designed to look like everyone's favorite stoner towel, Towelie, but there's also an Arctis Nova 5 Pro headset in the same light purple, featuring his silly face on the earcups. If you're more of a fan of the main cast, though, there's a version of the QcK L with funny portraits of Cartman, Stan, Kyle, and Kenny, too.

BlackLyte may not have the same name recognition as Secretlab, but the company has landed some pretty unique collaborations for its Athena Pro gaming chair . Not only does it have a compelling array of game-themed options, including the likes of Wuchang: Fallen Feathers and Rainbow Six Seige, but it's also a great choice for those looking to rep well-established eSports teams, such as Team Spirit, Team Fnatic, Team Liquid, and more. If you're looking for a mid-range gaming chair with some fun aesthetics, you could do a whole lot worse than these vibrant offerings.

If you're a fan of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, it's hard not to be impressed by Ghost's TMNT lineup . The company's Sentinel series chair comes in a sweet Leonardo special edition that has his iconic blue bandana across the head pillow. And while the special editions of the Wraith M3 Pro gaming mouse and Banshee K68 HE keyboard may not land on our best gaming mouse or best gaming keyboard lists , they're certain to get the job done for folks who absolutely love the Turtles. Don't pass up the Oni deskpad, either, which features the full team in their fighting poses with the city skyline behind them. Cowabunga!

Corsair Call of Duty Black Ops 6 Collection

Love it or hate it, Call of Duty remains among the best-selling and most-played games on the market even decades after its first entry took the world by storm. Corsair knows what's up, too, and has provided players with some peripherals branded in the style of Black Ops 6 , one of the series' most well-received entries in recent years. Whether it's the HS80 headset or the rock solid M75 wireless mouse , these BO6 special editions are sure to satisfy Call of Duty enthusiasts looking for a sleek but visually striking set of peripherals.

Billy Givens is a freelancer at IGN with over a decade of experience writing gaming, film, and tech content. His work can also be found on GameSpot, USA Today, Digital Trends, Tom's Guide, and more. You'll find him blabbering on about video games and more on Twitter at @mektige.

articles.title: [UPDATE] GTA 6 Leaker Releases Even More Gameplay Videos as People Spend Hundreds of Dollars to Vote on Next Leak, Fueling Crypto Scheme
articles.summary: The GTA 6 leaker has continued to release new gameplay clips, and is even running a poll to decide which video to leak next despite Rockstar parent company Take-Two's ongoing hunt for people responsible.
articles.body:
UPDATE AUGUST 24, 2026: The GTA 6 leaker has continued to release new gameplay clips, and is even running a poll to decide which video to leak next despite Rockstar parent company Take-Two's ongoing hunt for people responsible.

A tenth leaked GTA 6 video was released last night, this time showing plane at night gameplay. There is no cutscene footage this time.

The watermarks are the same as those on the previous video, advertising the 'CyberLeek' token at the heart of the cryptocurrency scheme that is believed to be the motivating factor behind all this. Another watermark doubles down on the anti-all-digital future manifesto that formed part of the initial CyberLeek website. It reads: "They want to take your right to resell. The peaceful route got us nowhere. This was plotted by them for years. It is time to fight now or never."

Meanwhile, CyberLeek has a new poll available on its website with a number of gameplay video choices people can vote on by sending tokens. People are currently spending hundreds of dollars' worth of the token to vote .

This poll ends today, August 24, which suggests the leaker or leakers intend to continue to release gameplay videos even in the face of Take-Two's subpoenas of Microsoft, Discord, and X / Twitter as part of the company's hunt for identifying information.

We are now into the sixth consecutive day of CyberLeek releases in what has been one of the most remarkable video game leaks of all time. It is now just a few days until Rockstar's official GTA 6 reveal, exclusive to Netflix for six hours.

UPDATE AUGUST 23, 2026: The GTA 6 leaks have stretched into a sixth consecutive day, as the person or group responsible shows no sign of slowing down even in the face of court action from Rockstar parent company Take-Two.

The latest leak is the ninth GTA 6 gameplay video to emerge this week from the 'CyberLeek' persona. It shows one of the two protagonists, Jason, driving to a gas station to cause havoc. There he steals a pickup truck from a conspiracy theorist. The video ends with another brief look at the same cutscene shown in the gameplay videos that were leaked yesterday.

And, as with all the leaked GTA 6 videos, this "gas" clip advertises the 'CyberLeek' token at the heart of the cryptocurrency scheme that is believed to be the motivating factor behind all this. A new watermark doubles down on the anti-all-digital future manifesto that formed part of the initial CyberLeek website. It reads: "They want to take your right to resell. The peaceful route got us nowhere. This was plotted by them for years. It is time to fight now or never."

In other related news. Take-Two lawyers have issued a subpoena to X / Twitter to identify the person or persons behind three accounts that contain 'CyberLeak' within them. This subpoena follows two filed earlier this week requesting information from Microsoft and Discord.

ORIGINAL STORY AUGUST 22, 2026: The alleged GTA 6 leaker has released two further gameplay videos despite Rockstar owner Take-Two's subpoenas requesting identifying information from Microsoft and Discord.

The ‘CyberLeek’ person or group released two new videos today, August 22, one showing more supercar gameplay and an armed robbery, the other strip club gameplay. The latter appears to taunt Take-Two and Rockstar by showing a snippet of a cutscene in which a character says they need to take "a leak." This is the second cutscene to emerge this week, and there is growing concern that the leaker has access to a build of the game and may post significant story spoilers.

These new videos are the seventh and eighth to leak this week. And, like all the others , they advertise the ‘CyberLeek’ memecoin as part of what is widely considered to be a crypto scheme .

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

On August 20, Take-Two issued Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) subpoenas in a federal court requesting information from both Microsoft and Discord as part of its hunt for the leaker or leakers behind the recent spate of GTA 6 gameplay videos. Take-Two wants identifying information associated with user accounts that were members of a number of Discord servers, including one relating to Australian GTA content creator Matthew "Matt" Judge, aka DarkViperAU. Judge has denied any wrongdoing .

Meanwhile, Take-Two issued Github with a DMCA takedown notice on Wednesday, August 19, saying “the infringer is sharing the stolen content from our copyright.” The takedown notice added: “The entire repository must be completely disabled, there are no remedies to rectify this clear case of infringement.” Via the subpoenas, Take-Two wants to identify those responsible for posting the leaks on Github, as well as “all internal Microsoft business records and investigative records associated with Microsoft’s internal investigation of the ‘cyberleek’ persona sufficient to identify the user(s), person(s) and/or entity/ies associated with that persona.”

The United States District Court for the Southern District of New York granted the Microsoft subpoena on August 21. Last night, Xbox Chief Technical Officer Scott Van Vliet tweeted to address the situation, saying: "We are working closely with Take-Two and Rockstar Games to support efforts to protect creative works and intellectual property."

Discord told Variety : “Discord sometimes receives subpoenas related to the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA). We review and comply with valid subpoenas when we receive them, as is standard and routine for companies like ours.”

Neither Rockstar nor Take-Two have issued a statement. IGN has asked for comment.

According to Bloomberg , Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift next week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events.

Undeterred, Netflix tweeted to tease Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look , which is set for Thursday, August 27, and will remain exclusive on the streaming platform for six hours before it makes its way to other platforms such as YouTube.

GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto VI exists in its own universe
articles.summary: Even a slew of “cyberleek” clips popping up across social media and a Netflix timed-exclusive gameplay reveal can’t stop the GTA VI momentum.
articles.body: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on GTA VI and the state of the video game industry, follow Andrew Webster. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started Four years ago, fans got a long-awaited look at Grand Theft Auto VI with a huge cache of videos that showed off Rockstar’s latest open-world epic. There were 90 videos in total, providing a glimpse at the next-generation take on Vice City, introducing the game’s new dual protagonists, and generally showing off the crime-fueled mayhem the series is known for. The twist? This wasn’t some official reveal. The videos were part of a massive leak in September 2022 that ultimately ended with a life sentence in a secure hospital for the hacker, and they dropped months before Rockstar properly unveiled GTA VI to the world with its debut trailer. For many video game studios, a leak of that magnitude would be devastating. But not Rockstar: Following the unprecedented success of GTA V, which has sold more than 230 million copies across PC and three generations of consoles, it seems like there is little that can impact the studio in the lead-up to the sequel’s much-hyped launch. GTA VI’s first trailer was leaked less than a day before it was set to premiere in December 2023, and yet the official video went on to garner nearly 290 million views on YouTube.  That’s not all that has happened on the long road to launch. Outside of the leaks, the studio has also been accused of union busting, GTA VI has been delayed multiple times, and the game, which won’t be available on a disc, has been viewed as a worrying sign for the future of physical media. But none of that has done much to slow down Rockstar or the relentless force that is its next game. And next week the hype is poised to reach a new level: A gameplay trailer for GTA VI will premiere on Netflix, available to subscribers six hours before everyone else can watch it on YouTube. It’s a huge marketing coup, and the type of thing only GTA VI can get away with. How it’s going The lead-up to the Netflix premiere hasn’t exactly been smooth. Over the last week further leaks have spread unofficial gameplay clips across platforms like Discord and X, and Rockstar has flexed its legal muscles, subpoenaing both Microsoft and Discord in hopes of finding the culprit. This had led to some frustration internally, and potentially changes to how Rockstar approaches security, according to a Bloomberg report. But, once again, it doesn’t seem to have put a dent in the fervor around the game. GTA VI is so big that even small updates, like a cover art reveal, rack up millions of views. And this has allowed Rockstar to do things no one else can. It can reveal gameplay through a mainstream platform like Netflix, and maintain sustained interest in the game despite only releasing two trailers over the span of several years. “Grand Theft Auto reveals have become cultural moments in their own right,” Netflix exec Brandon Riegg said when announcing the gameplay reveal. “The anticipation and fandom around Grand Theft Auto VI is unprecedented, and we’re honored that Rockstar Games has partnered with us to debut the next part of the Grand Theft Auto story with Netflix members first.” This mentality isn’t entirely new for Rockstar, but the success of GTA V has allowed the studio to be more confident with how it reveals and launches games, eschewing the traditional news cycle in favor of, well, whatever it wants. Back in 2016, on a random Sunday afternoon, the studio released an image that was simply its logo on a red background. The internet promptly went into a craze, correctly surmising that Rockstar was teasing the next Red Dead Redemption, an open-world Western series that had been dormant for several years. That game, Red Dead Redemption 2, went on to sell nearly 90 million copies, giving Rockstar another blockbuster to fill the gap between GTAs. Open-world games have become widespread over the last decade or so, but there’s still no developer that renders its virtual worlds with the level of detail and realism that Rockstar does. That’s true whether we’re talking about a fictional version of modern California or the Wild West at the turn of the century. It’s also probably why the studio can get away with taking so long with GTA VI; fans have been given plenty of reason to believe that it’ll be worth the wait. And that’s why the steady stream of leaks has done little to diminish the hype around the game. In fact, they’re almost serving as a form of marketing; Rockstar may be content with a drip feed of news and details, but anxious fans are eager to soak up every new detail about the game, whether it’s official or not. What happens next Grand Theft Auto VI launches on November 19th, and it’s coming at a challenging time for the games industry. For basically everyone not named Nintendo, things are not looking good: Hardware is getting prohibitively expensive, physical media is dying, major platforms are in a state of upheaval, and ill-placed bets on live-service games have left the industry reeling. There are few signs that things will improve anytime soon. Amid all of that, GTA VI stands apart. It’s a launch so big that nearly every other major publisher and developer is getting out of its way, a game on a scale that has the potential to boost flagging console sales. GTA VI isn’t a fix for everything ailing the industry, and most of its benefits will be temporary for everyone but Rockstar and its parent company, Take-Two Interactive. There are also still plenty of questions ahead of its release, like what the future for the enduring multiplayer spinoff GTA Online looks like, or whether GTA VI’s satirical slant on Florida will still feel relevant after such a long development cycle. But for at least a few weeks later this year, players can pretend everything is normal while they lay waste to Vice City once again. By the way * Despite exploring new territory with the GTA VI gameplay reveal, Netflix appears to be slowly retreating from games. It recently closed two more internal studios, including the team behind the interactive horror story Unhinged. * Fired Rockstar workers are mired in a legal battle with Rockstar, but they say they currently aren’t calling for a boycott of GTA VI. * November is mostly quiet for non-GTA releases, but there’s one game that isn’t afraid to go up against the behemoth: The Binding of Isaac: Repentance + Online. Read this * The Guardian’s “Pushing Buttons” newsletter looks at the challenges presented by hyperrealistic games like GTA VI. * Friend of The Verge Joshua Rivera has a great piece in Aftermath looking at how GTA VI’s outsize importance is a terrible thing for the industry at large. * Bloomberg has an interview with Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick about GTA VI’s “unprecedented” preorder numbers.

articles.title: Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 Controller Is Still Available for Preorder (But It May Sell Out)
articles.summary: The Marvel's Wolverine-themed PS5 controller has been a huge bestseller among the IGN audience, but it may be starting to sell out ahead of release.
articles.body:
The big PS5 exclusive this fall is Marvel’s Wolverine. It’s Insomniac Studios’ follow-up to the excellent (and massively successful) Spider-Man games, and it promises to be a bloody good time . To go along with the game, Sony is releasing a series of limited-edition Marvel’s Wolverine-themed PS5 hardware . Among IGN readers, by far the most popular item has been the Battle Yellow DualSense Wireless Controller. And while preorders have sold out at some retailers, it’s still available at most of them ( see it at Amazon ). It costs $89.99 and is set to release on September 15, the same day as the game.

Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Controller

DualSense Wireless Controller – Marvel’s Wolverine Battle Yellow Limited Edition

Functionally, Marvel’s Wolverine Limited-Edition PS5 DualSense Wireless Controller is a standard PS5 controller. What makes it stand out is the design, which makes it look like Wolverine got mad while playing Fortnite and attacked the thing. It features three jagged claw marks across the face of the controller. The marks are vibrant yellow, set against the black of the grips and touchpad. It looks fierce.

The bottom of the controller is also yellow, as are the shapes on the face buttons and the tiny arrows on the D-pad. On the left and right grips you’ll also find gray scuff marks that add to the battle-damage effect. Overall, it’s one of the coolest PS5 controller designs yet — and there have been a lot .

Marvel’s Wolverine Limited Edition PS5 Console Bundle and Accessories

The controller actually comes in two variations. There’s a “Battle Yellow” one that’s bright and bold. Then there’s an “Adamantium” white one that features the same scuffed-and-clawed design, but with metallic white to accent the black, making it somewhat less flashy. The Adamantium white one was a PlayStation Direct exclusive, and it has, unfortunately, sold out.

Both designs also have matching console covers you can buy separately, though some of those have sold out as well (the Battle Yellow PS5 slim console cover is still in stock at PS Direct ). It’s possible PS Direct will get more in stock before launch, but I wouldn’t hold my breath. If you want any of these items, you’d be wise to make your purchase sooner than later.

For more, check out our Marvel's Wolverine preorder guide to get the rundown on what preorder bonuses you can expect if you lock in a copy of the game early.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's board game and LEGO coverage. You can follow him on Bluesky .

articles.title: HBO's Lanterns Holds Strong in Episode 2, Proving It's One of the Best DCU Projects So Far
articles.summary: Lanterns continues to impress in its sophomore episode, proving that Kyle Chandler’s Hal and Aaron Pierre’s John are just as entertaining apart as they are together. Read our full review of Episode 2.
articles.body:
Warning: This review contains full spoilers for Lanterns Season 1, Episode 2!

Lanterns got a lot of things right in its pilot episode , but above all, the series benefited from the compelling chemistry between Kyle Chandler's Hal Jordan and Aaron Pierre's John Stewart. These two can barely tolerate one another at the best of times, and it makes for a hell of a lot of fun. But what happens when the follow-up episode splits this Dynamic Duo up for the majority of its runtime? As it turns out, these two characters are just as fascinating apart as they are together.

Episode 2 features some terrific Hal/John scenes as bookends, but for the most part, the emphasis is on the two men as solo players. While John carries out a glorified fetch quest for his grouchy mentor, Hal sets about digging deeper into the mysteries of Rushville, Nebraska. Needless to say, both men wind up discovering far more than they bargained for in the end.

Chandler continues to be pitch-perfect as this extremely onerous take on the iconic DC hero, but anyone this prickly really needs someone to serve as his foil. Luckily, Sheriff Kerry (Kelly Macdonald) is able to slot into that role nicely. Her acerbic banter with Hal is every bit as entertaining as the core Hal/John rivalry. This episode also allows us to sympathize with both sides of that dynamic. We can certainly feel Kerry's frustration as she deals with Hal's nonsense (including pulling him over with a car full of lukewarm corpses). At the same time, Hal proves that he's once again right to be suspicious that strange things are afoot in this sleepy town. His gut truly doesn't lie.

One thing Episode 2 really gets across is just how much of a comedy Lanterns is, on top of being a gritty murder mystery where the costumed characters drop F-bombs with abandon. This installment is surprisingly, almost aggressively funny. A lot of that is thanks to Hal's impromptu detective work, but credit also goes to John as he roams the halls of Hal's empty mansion and meets "Earl" for the first time. Pierre is great at playing the calm, collected straight man while everything gets progressively more surreal around him.

I noted in my previous review that I wasn't overly enamored with the actual murder mystery at play. Thankfully, this episode is able to add some wrinkles to said mystery, enough to spice things up a bit. For one thing, we discover that Kerry was a lot more keyed in on the alien situation from the get-go than she let on, and it's increasingly clear that something is rotten beneath the small town facade. For another, we get a taste of the other half of the equation thanks to the debut of Antaan (Paul Ben-Victor) and his men.

Granted, it's a little frustrating that so many alien characters in this series are conveniently taking human form. It does make Lanterns feel a bit more limited in scope than I'd like. Even so, all the talk of rogue Manhunters and ruined civilizations does help elevate the conflict beyond just a simple small-town shootout. And I’m also enjoying how much these episodes are relying on subtle dialogue cues to clue us into the fact that these characters aren’t who they appear to be. There was the whole interrogation scene last week, and now the proximity/closeness exchange between John and Antaan.

Episode 2 ends on a particularly strong note, as Hal and John reunite at the motel. Their exchange is compelling. We watch as John silently wrestles with the question of whether he can truly trust Hal, and then throws caution to the wind and lets out everything he learned from Antaan. Maybe there’s hope for this duo after all.

Or maybe not. The episode ends with a hard pivot into more cosmic DC territory, as Hal finally suits up for the first time in 2016 and flies to Oa to pay a call on the incarcerated Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen). We only get a few tantalizingly brief lines between the two characters, but I’m eagerly looking forward to seeing how this conversation plays out. Sinestro is easily one of my favorite DC villains, and the series can only benefit by leaning more into the larger-than-life trappings of the Green Lantern franchise.

articles.title: Peggy Carter Getting 'Frisbeed to Death' in Doctor Strange Was 'A Complete Disservice,' Hayley Atwell Says
articles.summary: Peggy Carter's untimely demise in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was a "complete disservice to the character," Marvel actress Hayley Atwell has said.
articles.body:
After years of waiting to become a superhero herself, Peggy Carter's untimely demise in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness was a "complete disservice to the character," Marvel actress Hayley Atwell has said.

Speaking at the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London this weekend, Atwell said that she had tried to pitch alternate versions of her character's fight to the death against Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff/Scarlet Witch, only for her suggestions to be ignored.

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness features an alternate version of Peggy Carter who has become Captain Carter, and wields a version of Captain America's shield that sports a Union Jack logo. Sadly, alongside the rest of her Illuminati (Illumi-what-y?) team, she is quickly wiped out by Wanda.

Marvel Cinematic Universe: Every Upcoming Movie and TV Show

"I loved the idea that she'd be in the suit and have the shield," Atwell began. "And if I'm really brutally honest, I was so disappointed with how they positioned her and what happened to her in that scene. It's so small, and she gets frisbeed to death."

Of course, the point of her character's presence in the movie is to demonstrate Wanda's power and to show how far the former Avenger has fallen as she wipes out a team of heroes, including Carter, John Krasinski's Mr. Fantastic, and Patrick Stewart's Professor X.

But it's also true that Atwell gets just a handful of lines before Wanda appears and kills them all within seconds. There's a fun moment where Carter gets to quote Steve Rogers' classic "I could do this all day" line, but, seconds later, Wanda sends Captain Carter's shield bouncing back into the heroine's gut, with the suggestion she has been bisected completely.

Atwell says it was the quoting of Steve Rogers' dialogue that particularly irked her, as the obvious response was then "no you couldn't [do this all day]," prompting the feeling that actually she was just "lame."

"I felt that was like a bum steer and a complete disservice to the character," Atwell added. "I tried on set to kind of go, 'Can I just add? Can I just suggest?' And they were like, 'Sure, but no.'"

Atwell will next return to the franchise in Avengers: Doomsday, and it'll be interested to see where the character goes next. Will there be a chance for Carter to suit up again, or will she be left at home holding the baby? (Even if it is the latter, this is probably preferable to Doctor Doom holding it instead.) Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters on December 18, and Marvel has put together a list of MCU movies and TV shows you should watch before it arrives .

articles.title: Billie Piper Says She's 'Not the Next Doctor' After That Bizarre Doctor Who Cliffhanger, Asks Fans to 'Chill Out'
articles.summary: Billie Piper has finally discussed her bizarre Doctor Who cliffhanger, and said "everyone needs to chill out and wait" while the show is on hiatus.
articles.body:
Billie Piper has finally discussed her bizarre Doctor Who cliffhanger, and said "everyone needs to chill out and wait" while the show is on hiatus.

Piper appeared in the closing seconds of last season following the regeneration of Ncuti Gatwa's Doctor, though exactly who she was playing was left deliberately unclear. Was she the Doctor's next regeneration, or a version of her previous character, the beloved companion Rose Tyler?

Speculation around her appearance was fuelled by reports that it was a last-minute addition to the series, amid uncertainty over its future. Indeed, the finale's last third consisted of scenes added in reshoots, as Gatwa had quit the show and required some form of exit sequence.

Now, more than a year on, Doctor Who's future seems no more secure. The BBC has said it will put the franchise's production up for tender, a process in which external companies can bid to make the series. However, several more months have passed since this announcement, and last week Doctor Who writer Mark Gatiss stated that the series' return would "quietly won't happen" as it now needed to be rested.

The 25 Most Essential Doctor Who Episodes

With all this in mind, it's no wonder that Piper was quizzed about her future in Doctor Who at this weekend's For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London. And while the actress remained fairly tight-lipped, she did confirm that she was "not the next Doctor" in waiting.

"I am not the next Doctor, I am Rose Tyler in hiatus," Piper said. "Sorry that's a really cryptic answer but because I'm not currently filming Doctor Who as the Doctor I can't lie and say otherwise. I'm sweating, I hate this.

"I think you've all gotta be very patient," she continued. "It'll be worth it when it comes. I think what we need to celebrate is the show the fact has been on air for 26 years, the new incarnation. It's been around a very long time, it's massively successful and it's impacted so many people's lives positively. It's had a bit of a rough time lately and I think everyone needs to chill out and wait for what comes from having this space and time."

Piper mentioning the show's recent "rough time" appears to be a reference to the series' production struggles in the wake of previous co-funding partner Disney losing interest in the show, in the wake of middling ratings and criticism of its quality. Showrunner Russell T. Davies and existing production company Bad Wolf both confirmed they would no longer be part of the series' future earlier this year, at the same time as the BBC confirmed its intention to put the series out to tender.

A previous report by Deadline suggested there was now hesitation among production companies to take on Doctor Who , despite — or perhaps because of — its legendary status. "You would have to be mad," one source said. "[It's a] bit of a nightmare for any producer in this market with the shadow of the Disney fallout ," said another. A third suggested the series' budget would likely be around $3 million per episode — half of the budget for the episodes Disney previously funded, inviting difficult comparisons.

All of which tallies with comments from former Doctor Who Magazine editor Tom Spilsbury, who last year suggested it would likely be "five or six years before we see anything new," as the series' next incarnation is determined. "At which point, it will be the children of 2005 who will be bringing the show back, just as Russell predicted. As ever, time will tell."

articles.title: Former Rockstar Dev Calls GTA 6 Leaks 'A Nothing Burger,' Insists Hot Coffee Was Much, Much Worse
articles.summary: As Take-Two works to identify the person or group behind the GTA 6 'CyberLeek' account, one former Rockstar developer has insisted the recent spate of gameplay leaks will have little impact on the success of the game itself.
articles.body:
As Take-Two works to identify the person or group behind the GTA 6 'CyberLeek' account, one former Rockstar developer has insisted the recent spate of gameplay leaks will have little impact on the success of the game itself.

CyberLeek has released 10 GTA 6 gameplay videos and an image of the full map in the space of just six days , sparking a manhunt for the people responsible. Rockstar parent company Take-Two has subpoenaed Microsoft, Discord, and even X / Twitter, but the leaker appears undeterred, and is even running a crypto-fueled poll to determine which video to release next.

All this just a week before Netflix’s timed-exclusive reveal of GTA 6, which is set to fully unveil the game officially for the first time.

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

From a Take-Two and Rockstar perspective, significant damage is being done. According to Bloomberg , Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say the Hot Coffee scandal was much more damaging than these GTA 6 leaks.

“Calm down everybody. The leaks are a nothing burger,” Vermeij began.

“As a marketing strategy R* is trying to keep the game under wraps longer than other publishers. All that has happened is that some footage has escaped. Slightly ahead of the Netflix thing next week.

“90% of future players don’t spend their time on the internet looking for video snippets. They don’t have the time and don’t want spoilers.

“I imagine the teams are a little annoyed about it but not more than that. I was there during Hot Coffee. It was a nightmare for management (R*NewYork) but didn’t affect us (R*North) much. The current leaks are far less consequential than HC was.

“It looks like GTA 6 will be phenomenal and sell for the next 15 years or so. The leaks are just a tiny blip.”

The Hot Coffee scandal was a 2005 controversy involving a hidden, sexually explicit mini-game inside Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. Modders discovered that unfinished code left on game discs allowed players to unlock a crude, interactive sex scene, leading to political outrage, a temporary "Adults Only" rating, and multimillion-dollar settlements for Rockstar Games.

“No, it really hurt,” Vermeij said of Hot Coffee. “The game had to be withdrawn from stores in the USA. It could only be sold as 18+ until the new version was ready. It is estimated to have cost $50 million which was a lot of money for R*/T2 at the time.”

Speaking to Lex Fridman in October last year , Rockstar co-founder Dan Houser said the company “nearly imploded several times due to Hot Coffee,” adding: “It was extremely tough.”

There is growing concern that CyberLeek may spoil the GTA 6 story by releasing plot-critical cutscenes. So far, that hasn’t happened, but even if it did, Vermeij downplayed the impact. “That would suck but people will still play it,” he said.

There is also speculation that CyberLeek has a working build of GTA 6, based on some of the gameplay shown in the leaks. “If that is the case it probably only runs on a devkit,” Vermeij insisted. “Devkits have more memory. There probably isn't a build in existence that would run on a retail PS5 at the moment.”

GTA 6 is expected to be the biggest entertainment launch of all time, setting records for sales and revenue. As Vermeij says, the gameplay leaks are unlikely to threaten the success of the game's November launch. But they remain part of what is a significant security breach for Take-Two and Rockstar, one that will no doubt affect the morale of staff who have spent years building the game. They also potentially dampen the impact of the timed-exclusive reveal on Netflix, which I imagine isn't thrilled by what's going on.

Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar has issued a statement on the GTA 6 leaks. IGN has asked for comment.

Wesley is Director, News at IGN. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: Exclusive: PokémonXP and 2026 Pokémon World Championships Pokémon Center Merch Reveal
articles.summary: See a huge selection of Pokémon merch to be exclusively sold at the 2026 Pokémon World Championships and PokémonXP pop-up Pokémon Center, including a Steiff Pikachu, a rocket backpack, and more.
articles.body:
The 2026 Pokémon World Championships are right around the corner in San Francisco, California on August 28–30, and that means a new coveted Pokémon merchandise drop at its exclusive pop-up Pokémon Center. This isn’t just any year, though — it’s also Pokémon’s 30th Anniversary and the first-ever official Pokémon fan-convention, PokémonXP . The Pokémon Company is going all-out with the collections this year, and we’ve got an exclusive first look at what to expect at the combo 2026 Worlds and PokémonXP Pokémon Center, including a unique stuffed Pikachu made by the inventors of the Teddy Bear, Steiff.

Before we get into everything else — and trust me, there’s a lot — take a good look at this Steiff 2026 Pokémon World Championships Exclusive Pikachu. This isn’t the classic stuffed toy company’s first take on Pikachu, as they produced one in 2015 and another just this July celebrating Pokémon’s 30th Anniversary , but this Steiff Pikachu is the first accessorized edition!

We can’t be certain of the 2026 Pokémon World Championships Exclusive Pikachu collectible’s materials and price, but Steiff’s previous Pikachu renditions were made of premium natural mohair and sold for around $400.

Senior director of Pokémon Center and e-commerce Cindy Ruppenthal explains: “As one of the standout items for this year, fans can only receive it via voucher — meaning, those booking a store reservation can opt in to enter the selection process to purchase fan-favorite items.”

Like at last year’s Pokémon World Championships in Anaheim, California, PokémonXP and the Pokémon World Championships this year feature three distinct merch lines.

“To celebrate this year’s San Francisco location, Pokémon Center will be releasing three product lines — the PokémonXP Line, the 2026 Pokémon World Championships Line, and the San Francisco Line,” Ruppenthal said.

Without further ado, let’s take a look at some of the exclusive merch you can try to snag at this year’s event.

PokémonXP heavily features blue space-themed items, like the previously revealed female Pikachu dressed in clothing fit for a star-exploring astronaut. (We know she’s female because of her heart-shaped tail!) A goggles- and jetpack-wearing Charizard accompanies space Pikachu as a co-mascot of this line, and is featured in its own figure, wall art, and more. I personally love the dark shirt with Charizard on it, but am predicting the pastel blue bomber jacket decorated with on-theme patches and the baseball jersey will be among the more popular clothing. Finally, don’t miss the Rocket backpack, one of the most unique items revealed so far.

I had to ask, “Why space?” Ruppenthal explained the team used “Out of This World” as the driving concept behind both the designs and experiences this year–hoping that together, PokémonXP and the 2026 World Championships deliver a weekend that takes fans “somewhere truly out of this world.”

Glow in the Dark Line - 2026 Pokemon World Championships Pokemon Center

To go with the space theme even further, the PokémonXP line features exciting glow-in-the-dark items featuring the oft-adored Umbreon and otherworldly Elgyem. They seem like they’d be right at home with the glow-in-the-dark stars I had on my ceiling when I was a kid.

As hard as this is to believe across decades of products, Ruppenthal said this is Pokémon Center’s first-ever glow-in-the-dark collection, and the eye-catching designs light up in the dark after first being exposed to a light source, like sunlight, an LED flashlight, or a UV blacklight.

Ruppenthal said that alongside things like the glow-in-the-dark collection and Rocket backpack, there’s another new concept debuting this year: Lava flow glitter pins, which feature liquid in the actual pins to add depth. It looks like the Charizard pin from this collection is one of those.

Pokemon World Championships Line - 2026 Pokemon Center

The World Championships line features a regal-looking male Pikachu plush with a champion’s cape and crown, who also appears on a variety of items like shirts, bags, hats, TCG accessories, and more. Greninja is highlighted in this line, appearing alongside the kingly Pikachu on the double deck box, and on its own collectible pin, light-up display, and hat. The Worlds line is primarily an orange-red hue, and you’ll find the classic Pokémon World Championships logo and the 2026 San Francisco logo on many of these items.

San Francisco Line - 2026 Pokemon World Championships Pokemon Center

You’ll find eclectic, colorful line drawings featured in the San Francisco line. I personally love the busy playmat with so many little things to discover. The cream-colored ringer tee is a cute departure from the classic t-shirt, and its matching Krabby hat makes for a nice set, too.

“The San Francisco Line reimagines the city through a Pokémon lens, blending the PokémonXP 'Out of This World' design theme with iconic San Francisco architecture transformed by Pokémon-inspired elements,” Ruppenthal explained. “Some fun artwork fans can look for include Poké Ball details on the Painted Ladies, a Gigantamax Duraludon-inspired variation of the Transamerica Pyramid, Poké Ball-inspired cable cars, and a Technical Machine (TM).”

“Fans can also discover Pokémon woven through the playmat design, including Pikachu, Vileplume, Krabby, Ditto, Umbreon, Espeon, Latias, Latios, Jirachi, and many more — adding even more Pokémon-inspired details for fans to discover,” Ruppenthal said.

“Inspired by the bright and vibrant spirit of the city, each unique line captures the energy and character of San Francisco while bringing a distinctly Pokémon twist,” Ruppenthal said. “And because this is a milestone year, fans may even spot exclusive items featuring a mix of both the PokémonXP Line and the 2026 Pokémon World Championships Line…”

Perfect for the indecisive (me), this mix "line" (not a distinct line) has items that commemorate both events and the location, all in one. Expect both the bold blues of PokémonXP and the fiery reds of the Pokémon World Championships with design-inspo from the San Francisco line. The keychain has charms for all three line logos and both mascot Pikachu, the pin-set has both mascot Pikachu and the San Francisco-inspired cable car and Pokémon-ified Painted Ladies.

One standout item in this collection is the collectible coins set, which comes with nine coins, each with a different Pokémon featured in the merch this year.

Finally, we’re once again getting a new Reyn Spooner collection, a now annual tradition started at the 2024 Pokémon World Championships in Honolulu. Fitting, considering the brand is designed in Hawaii. You can find Reyn Spooner collab items at the online Pokémon Center store now, but these particular aloha shirt, hat, and bag designs will be exclusive to the event in San Francisco. I have one of the 2025 Pokémon World Championships Reyn Spooner tote bag from Anaheim, and I love it. It's the perfect beach bag, deep with lots of internal pockets, a clip for your keys, and a big zipper to keep everything secure. I'm currently using it to store my overflow of deckboxes and bulk cards, which means I have an excuse to get this one to dedicate to outdoor activities.

Previously, The Pokémon Company revealed the two Pikachu mascot, Charizard, and Kirlia plushies. Bear Walker also revealed there will be two new skateboards this year, one for PokémonXP and one for the Pokémon World Championships. We assume you’ll need to opt into the drawing to receive a voucher to be able to buy the Bear Walker Skateboards, like you did at Worlds in Anaheim last year.

Previously Revealed 2026 Pokemon Worlds and PokemonXP Merch

As for the design of the Pokémon Center this year, Ruppenthal said the store design "seamlessly blends both events, while also celebrating the city’s unique character, iconic landmarks, and local charm through a Pokémon-inspired lens." Each line will also have "its own moment to shine."

You’ll need a PokémonXP / Pokémon World Championships badge to get into the Pokémon Center pop-up, and you’ll also need to have signed up for a timeslot. However, there will be a “Worlds at Home” online-only “shopping experience” beginning August 26, Ruppenthal said, but it’s a mystery to what exactly that will entail.

Last year, there was a code to get the Worlds Promo Card with purchase, and a different code to get the collectible Worlds Coin with at least a $50 purchase . There was also a new line of products that simultaneously launched online and at the Pokémon Center pop-up–the Sweetheart Diner collection.

You can also get your hands on the 2026 Worlds Pikachu promo card by participating in a Worlds Celebration Tournament at Play! Pokémon Store events — either VGC with Pokémon Champions or the TCG — from August 21–30.

PokémonXP and the 2026 Pokémon World Championships are in just a few days, and we’ll be there! In the meantime, for more on Pokémon, check out some of the coolest and rarest Pokémon items in IGN staff’s collections (including mine, which is a lot of old Worlds merch), and why the 2026 Pokémon North American International Championship is moving from New Orleans .

Casey DeFreitas is the deputy editor of guides at IGN, and has attended the Pokémon World Championships since 2017. Catch her on socials @ShinyCaseyD , and at Worlds!

articles.title: GTA 6 Leaker Drops New Nudity-Filled Gameplay, Polls People on Whether to Release Story Spoilers
articles.summary: The past week's extraordinary set of GTA 6 leaks appear to have continued today with a significant new release of footage that depicts mass nudity. Meanwhile, the leaker has suggested story spoilers could be posted next, and has called on fans to protest outside the offices of Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive.
articles.body:
The past week's extraordinary set of GTA 6 leaks appear to have continued today with a significant new release of footage that depicts mass nudity. Meanwhile, the leaker has suggested story spoilers could be posted next, and has called on fans to protest outside the offices of Rockstar and Take-Two Interactive.

Today's newly-posted footage from the 'CyberLeek' person or group depicts GTA 6 main character Jason exploring a "nudist town" area filled with naked characters. Male and female genitalia are both fully exposed. Explicit dialogue can be heard as the NPCs party, while the player uses binoculars to zoom in on character models. This action eventually results in a fight breaking out, leading to the player ultimately gunning numerous civilians down.

While the amount of nudity on screen is surprising, the footage is perhaps even more notable for its watermarked message, which claims that footage of a "Lucia-led prologue" could be released next. Once again, the leaker calls for fans to vote on what they should release — cast by spending cryptocurrency that earns the leaker(s) money , it's important to note, something that is widely believed to be a crypto scheme .

Every Detail in the GTA 6 Cover Art Explained

Bizarrely, the leaker also calls for a physical show of support from those watching, and states that they want "gamers" dressed up as leeks to hold up game discs while standing outside Rockstar offices in protest.

This marks another significant escalation by those responsible for the leaks, who have called for real-world action for the first time. Additionally, it's worth stating that the gameplay released to date has included two snippets of cutscenes that feature no significant story details, and mostly focus on open-world gameplay of Jason. It seems far more significant footage of the game may leak next.

The leaker also seems to be attempting to highlight their initially-stated reason for the leaks, as a form of protest against the decision not to offer GTA 6 via a physical disc, something that was announced just days before PlayStation revealed it would kill PS5 game discs for new games released from January 2028 onwards.

All of this comes just ahead of Netflix's exclusive "reveal" of GTA 6 gameplay footage via its Grand Theft Auto 6: An Extended Look , which is set for Thursday, August 27, and will remain exclusive on the streaming platform for six hours before it makes its way to other platforms such as YouTube.

According to Bloomberg , Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff. Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks .

GTA 6 is due out on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S on November 19, 2026. Take-Two has subpoenaed Microsoft, Discord, and even X / Twitter, but the leaker appears undeterred. IGN has asked Take-Two and Rockstar for comment.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Trailer Gets Frame-by-Frame Official LEGO Remake
articles.summary: Marvel Studios has recreated the Avengers: Doomsday trailer frame-by-frame in LEGO, bringing Doctor Doom and Earth's Mightiest Heroes to life brick-by-brick.
articles.body:
IGN can exclusively reveal an official LEGO-inspired version of the trailer for Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday .

The trailer – created by Disney Consumer Products, Marvel Studios and LEGO as part of their “All Moments Lead to Doomsday” campaign – can be watched below.
